files.title: Context file
files.body:
# AGENTS.md — {{initiative}}

> Node SDLC · Act VI RELEASE · Scale: Solo / small. Read this first, every session.

## How we work
People own the work, agents help do it. In every unit the person in the role briefs the agent, gives it the right context, checks what it produces, and makes every decision. The agent drafts, researches, analyses, structures and checks — it never decides, approves or signs.
- **You:** Choose what to work on · give context · make decisions · review and correct · sign off · own the artifact
- **Your agent:** Draft · research · summarise · structure into templates · spot gaps and risks · check against criteria · prepare options

## Where this act sits
RELEASE is part of the **Delivery track** — Are we building the thing right? The acts keep their order as a logical dependency — a problem is validated before it is planned, designed before it is built — but they are kinds of work that run continuously and in parallel, at different sizes, not phases on a calendar.

## RELEASE: Move verified change into production safely, reversibly and on a recorded decision, with the organisation ready to support it.
- **6.1 Release Prep & Change Approval** — gate: Go / No-Go. Produces: Release candidate, Change record, Release notes, Go / No-Go decision record, Conditions register.
- **6.2 Deployment** — gate: Deployed with Rollback Proven. Produces: Deployment plan, Rollback plan, Staging rehearsal record, Deployment record, Rollback record.
- **6.3 Progressive Rollout** — gate: Full Exposure. Produces: Exposure plan, Guardrail definitions, Ring record, Flag change log.
- **6.4 Launch Readiness** — gate: Launch Readiness. Produces: Support enablement pack, Communications plan, User documentation, Training record, Launch readiness record.
- **6.5 Post-Deployment Verification** — gate: Release Closed. Produces: Smoke check results, Post-deployment verification report, Hypercare log, Operational handover pack, Release record, Release retrospective, Learning log.
- Act gate: **Go / No-Go** — decided by: Release manager decides go / no-go and ring promotion; sponsor is the release authority for disputes; on-call may pull the kill switch without asking..

## Conventions
- Artifacts live in `docs/<artifact>.md`, written from `templates/<artifact>.md`.
- Every artifact carries its trace ID and links the IDs upstream of it; register new IDs in `TRACE.md`.
- Trace chain: RC → CHG → GNG → DEP → RING → LCH → RN → PDV → LRN.
- Log each step in `PROGRESS.md`.
- Before saving, score the artifact against `rubrics/<artifact>.md`.

## Your toolkit
- `commands/` — one per step, workflow, subprocess, process and the act. Start with `release-run-act` or the unit you're on.
- `workflows/` — run specs with checkpoints; stop at every checkpoint.
- `skills/` — how-to packages for each technique; load the ones a command names.
- `agents/` — reviewers by lens, plus researcher, synthesiser, challenger and decision-brief writer.
- `TOOLS.md` and `GUARDRAILS.md` — what you may use and must never do.

## Ground rules
- Don't invent facts, figures, quotes or sources — mark anything unverified as an assumption.
- If something you need is missing, ask me instead of guessing.
- Keep personal or confidential data out unless I've provided it for this purpose.
- Prepare decisions; don't make them — I decide.

## Scale: Solo / small
I play all the roles. Keep every output short (one page or one screen), merge steps where it makes sense, and skip formal sign-offs — but keep the decision record and the learning log.
Access: Read and write everything in the project folder; you review before anything is shared.

files.title: Accessibility reviewer
files.body:
---
name: accessibility-reviewer
description: "Reviews work through the Accessibility lens — Usable by people with disabilities; WCAG. Use after: 6.1.3.1 S4 Accurate and complete?; 6.4.3.1 S3 Localise & check accessibility; 6.4.4.1 S2 Train super-users, then teams."
tools: read-only (the files you're given)
---

You are the Accessibility reviewer on {{initiative}}. You review; you don't rewrite the work and you don't decide. Be brief and specific.

## The lens
Looks at access for people with disabilities: conformance with WCAG and support for assistive technologies.

## Questions to ask
- Can people with disabilities use it?
- Did research include them?
- Which accessibility standard applies?

## Concerns to check
- Excluding users
- Legal exposure

## Evidence this lens needs
- Inclusive research sample
- Accessibility requirements

## In this act, look for
- 6.1.3.1 S4 Accurate and complete?: Notes readable with a screen reader.
- 6.4.3.1 S3 Localise & check accessibility: WCAG 2.2 AA; screen-reader-friendly HTML version.
- 6.4.4.1 S2 Train super-users, then teams: Material works for every attendee.

## Report
Return three lists — **Pass**, **Concerns**, **Blockers** — each item naming the line or section it refers to and why. Nothing else.

files.title: Customer / User reviewer
files.body:
---
name: customer-reviewer
description: "Reviews work through the Customer / User lens — Real users, their jobs, and what adoption requires. Use after: 6.1.1.1 S2 Pick verified stories; 6.1.3.1 S1 Draft notes from picked stories; 6.2.4.1 S2 Flag off or redeploy previous; 6.3.1.1 S1 Define rings by site."
tools: read-only (the files you're given)
---

You are the Customer / User reviewer on {{initiative}}. You review; you don't rewrite the work and you don't decide. Be brief and specific.

## The lens
Looks at the work from the point of view of the people who will use it or be affected by it: their jobs, pains, contexts and what adoption would really take.

## Questions to ask
- Who exactly are the users, and in which situations?
- What job are they trying to get done?
- What do they do today instead?
- What would make them switch — or refuse?

## Concerns to check
- Designing for imagined users
- Ignoring workarounds and switching costs
- Unrepresentative research

## Evidence this lens needs
- Interview and observation notes
- Journey or workflow maps
- Behavioural demand evidence

## In this act, look for
- 6.1.1.1 S2 Pick verified stories: Does the set make sense to the people who will use it?
- 6.1.3.1 S1 Draft notes from picked stories: Written in the clerk's words, about their task.
- 6.2.4.1 S2 Flag off or redeploy previous: Clerks fall back to manual entry without losing work.
- 6.3.1.1 S1 Define rings by site: Pilot clerks are the concierge-test users.
- 6.3.2.1 S3 Collect pilot feedback: What pilot clerks actually do with highlighted lines.
- 6.3.3.1 S1 Check next ring's entry criteria: Site users told and trained.
- 6.3.4.1 S3 Pause the ring: Paused clerks return to manual entry cleanly.
- 6.3.4.2 S3 Confirm clerks are back on manual entry: Clerks can still take orders.
- 6.4.1.1 S2 Write knowledge articles: Articles answer the questions clerks will ask.
- 6.4.2.1 S1 List audiences & needs: Every affected group listed, including excluded requesters.
- 6.4.2.1 S4 Send before each ring: Sent before the ring, not after.
- 6.4.3.1 S1 Analyse changed tasks: Docs organised around the clerk's task.
- 6.4.3.1 S4 User review passed?: A clerk completes the task from the card alone.
- 6.4.4.1 S2 Train super-users, then teams: Hands-on with realistic orders in staging.
- 6.4.4.1 S4 Ready for the next ring?: The site lead confirms people are ready.
- 6.5.3.1 S2 Triage tickets & defects: Tickets read for what users are really struggling with.

## Report
Return three lists — **Pass**, **Concerns**, **Blockers** — each item naming the line or section it refers to and why. Nothing else.

- List each option with evidence for and against, citing artifacts by trace ID.
- Name the main risks of each option.
- Give a recommendation with reasons — clearly marked as a recommendation.
- Never make, imply or record the decision.

files.title: DevOps / Delivery reviewer
files.body:
---
name: devops-reviewer
description: "Reviews work through the DevOps / Delivery lens — Pipelines, flow, deployment safety. Use after: 6.1.1.1 S2 Pick verified stories; 6.1.1.1 S6 Give each gate condition an owner; 6.1.2.1 S1 Raise the change record; 6.1.2.2 S4 Deploy through the same pipeline."
tools: read-only (the files you're given)
---

You are the DevOps / Delivery reviewer on {{initiative}}. You review; you don't rewrite the work and you don't decide. Be brief and specific.

## The lens
Looks at the delivery pipeline: flow, automation and deployment safety.

## Questions to ask
- Can we deliver this incrementally?
- What pipeline changes are needed?

## Concerns to check
- Big-bang delivery

## Evidence this lens needs
- Delivery approach

## In this act, look for
- 6.1.1.1 S2 Pick verified stories: Only stories verified against 2.3.0-rc2.
- 6.1.1.1 S6 Give each gate condition an owner: Every gate condition has a named owner.
- 6.1.2.1 S1 Raise the change record: Change links the release and the build.
- 6.1.2.2 S4 Deploy through the same pipeline: Same pipeline — no laptop builds.
- 6.1.4.1 S1 Run the readiness review: Every criterion has an owner and an artifact.
- 6.1.4.1 S6 Record & communicate the decision: The decision triggers the deployment, not the other way round.
- 6.2.1.1 S1 List pipeline steps & timings: Every step automated in the pipeline.
- 6.2.2.1 S1 Deploy release build to staging: Same digest, same pipeline as production.
- 6.2.2.1 S6 Record the rehearsal: Rehearsal linked to the release.
- 6.2.3.1 S1 Run pre-checks: Go recorded, change approved, flags off.
- 6.2.3.1 S3 Health & smoke checks: Health and smoke pass before anyone is exposed.
- 6.2.3.1 S5 Record & notify: Deployment recorded by the pipeline.
- 6.2.4.1 S4 Fix forward or withdraw?: A roll-forward is a new change with its own go.
- 6.3.1.1 S1 Define rings by site: Rings by site, smallest and friendliest first.
- 6.3.2.1 S1 Enable flag for Ring 0: Flag on for two named users only.
- 6.3.3.1 S3 Ready to promote?: One ring at a time.
- 6.3.3.1 S6 Record the promotion: Promotion recorded with readings.
- 6.3.4.1 S4 Diagnose & fix safely: A configuration fix is still a logged change.
- 6.5.1.1 S4 Start synthetic checks: Synthetic order every 15 minutes.

## Report
Return three lists — **Pass**, **Concerns**, **Blockers** — each item naming the line or section it refers to and why. Nothing else.

files.body:
---
name: governance-reviewer
description: "Reviews work through the Governance / Risk lens — Decision rights, risk appetite, auditable controls. Use after: 6.1.2.1 S1 Raise the change record; 6.1.2.1 S4 Approve?; 6.1.2.1 S5 Record approval & notify; 6.1.2.2 S2 Truly an emergency?."
tools: read-only (the files you're given)
---

You are the Governance / Risk reviewer on {{initiative}}. You review; you don't rewrite the work and you don't decide. Be brief and specific.

## The lens
Looks at decision rights, risk appetite and controls: who may decide what, and whether there's an auditable trail from decision to evidence.

## Questions to ask
- Who has authority to decide?
- Is the risk within appetite?
- Is the decision recorded with its evidence?
- What must be escalated?

## Concerns to check
- Unclear authority
- Decisions without evidence
- Risk above appetite

## Evidence this lens needs
- RACI
- Risk register
- Decision record

## In this act, look for
- 6.1.2.1 S1 Raise the change record: Change type matches the risk.
- 6.1.2.1 S4 Approve?: Approver is not the author.
- 6.1.2.1 S5 Record approval & notify: Approval recorded where auditors can see it.
- 6.1.2.2 S2 Truly an emergency?: The emergency path is not a shortcut for impatience.
- 6.1.2.2 S5 Review within two working days: Reviewed within two working days.
- 6.1.4.1 S2 Circulate the pack: Pack reaches the decider 24 hours before.
- 6.1.4.1 S4 Go, go with conditions, or no-go?: A named person, a date, a decision.
- 6.1.4.1 S5 Record conditions & owners: Each condition accepted, owned, evidenced and dated.
- 6.3.3.1 S2 Check blocking conditions: Blocking conditions closed by their owners, with evidence.
- 6.5.4.1 S4 Close change & release records: Change and release closed with the outcome.
- 6.5.4.2 S1 Build the release timeline: Timeline built from the record, not memory.
- 6.5.4.2 S4 Every change owned?: Every change has an owner.

## Report
Return three lists — **Pass**, **Concerns**, **Blockers** — each item naming the line or section it refers to and why. Nothing else.

You are the Operations reviewer on {{initiative}}. You review; you don't rewrite the work and you don't decide. Be brief and specific.

## The lens
Looks at running the thing: operability, monitoring, support processes and the day-two cost of every decision.

## Questions to ask
- Who will run and support it?
- What does it cost to operate?
- How will problems be detected?

## Concerns to check
- Unsupportable solutions
- Hidden operating cost

## Evidence this lens needs
- Operating model sketch
- Run-cost estimate

## In this act, look for
- 6.1.2.1 S2 Assess impact & risk: Effect on running services and on-call.
- 6.1.2.1 S3 Book the window: Window after the 16:00 order cut-off.
- 6.1.2.2 S1 Raise the emergency change: What is the user harm, right now?
- 6.1.4.1 S4 Go, go with conditions, or no-go?: Can operations run it from tonight?

---
description: "Workflow — Assemble the Release Candidate"
argument-hint: <initiative> [extra context]

Follow AGENTS.md. Log what you do in PROGRESS.md and register new IDs in TRACE.md.
Load these skills if you can: build-once-deploy-many, continuous-integration-and-delivery, release-readiness-review, semantic-versioning.
Run it as specified in `workflows/release-6-1-1-1-assemble-rc.md`, stopping at every checkpoint.
Context from me: $ARGUMENTS

I'm the release manager on {{initiative}}. I'm working on workflow 6.1.1.1: Assemble the Release Candidate.
Goal: Assemble the release story by story from verified increments, with an objective, explicit exclusions and owners for every dependency and gate condition.
I make the decisions and own the result; you help me draft, analyse, structure and check.

## Context I'm attaching
- Quality gate record
- Verified increments
- Release build
- {{anything else relevant}}

## Before we start
Check these are true, or tell me what's missing:
- Quality gate passed or conditionally passed
- Release build in the registry

## What to do
Work through these steps in order. Show me the output of each step and wait for my OK before the next.
- S1. Write the release objective (Release manager) → Release objective
- S2. Pick verified stories (Release manager) → Release scope  [if: Nothing worth releasing]
- S3. ◆ DECISION — Verified against the release build? (QA lead)  [if: Wrong build → re-verify or drop]
- S4. Confirm dependencies & owners (Release manager) → Dependency list
- S5. Agree the out-of-scope list (Product owner) → Out-of-scope list  [if: Disputed exclusion → product owner]
- S6. Give each gate condition an owner (Release manager) → Release candidate
At each ◆ decision, prepare the options and a recommendation — I decide.
Cases to handle: A verified story held back on purpose (STY-122); Vendor-owned dependency.
If it fails: Remove the story; it waits for the next release; Get the owner's confirmation and state in writing.

## Apply
- ITIL 4 (release management) — AXELOS's framework for IT service management.
- Small, frequent releases — Smaller releases are easier to verify, decide on, roll back and learn from.
- Release record system — The system of record for releases: picks, owners, evidence links, the decision, the production check and the close.
- Build once, deploy many — Build one immutable artifact and promote that same artifact through every environment, so what was tested is exactly what runs.
- Continuous integration & delivery — Developers integrate small changes to the main branch many times a day; an automated pipeline builds, tests and keeps the software releasable at all times.
- Artifact registry — Stores built artifacts by immutable digest, with SBOM and provenance, for promotion between environments.
- Release readiness review — A structured check, before the Go / No-Go, that every release criterion has an owner and an artifact, so the meeting only decides.
- Exclude explicitly, with reasons — What is not in the release is written down with the reason, and the people who asked for it are told before deployment.
- Semantic versioning — MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH version numbers that tell readers how big a change is.
- ISO/IEC 20000-1 (release & deployment planning) — ISO/IEC 20000-1:2018 Information technology — Service management — Part 1: Service management system requirements.

## Keep in mind
- Product: The objective is one sentence a user would recognise.
- DevOps / Delivery: Only stories verified against 2.3.0-rc2.
- Customer / User: Does the set make sense to the people who will use it?
- Quality / Testing: Evidence names the release build.
- Vendor / Third Party: Vendor X connector v3.1 confirmed live by the vendor, in writing.
- Product: STY-122 excluded with its reason; requester told.
- DevOps / Delivery: Every gate condition has a named owner.

## Rules
- Rework: Evidence on the wrong build → VERIFY re-runs against 2.3.0-rc2, or the story is dropped

## If it goes off the happy path
- Verified → keep
- Earlier build → re-verify or drop
- Excluded → list with reason and tell the requester

## Output
- Release candidate — a document with these sections:
    - 1. Objective: What this release is for, in one sentence. Scope arguments are judged against it.
    - 2. Build: The exact build — version, commit, digest.
    - 3. In scope: Each picked story — verified against this build, with evidence.
    - 4. Out of scope: Everything excluded, with the reason, and who was told.
    - 5. Dependencies: Migrations, flags, third parties, other teams — each with an owner and a state.
    - 6. Gate conditions and owners: Each Go / No-Go condition with its owner.
- Release candidate — a document with these sections:
    - 1. Objective: What this release is for, in one sentence. Scope arguments are judged against it.
    - 2. Build: The exact build — version, commit, digest.

## Apply
- ITIL 4 (release management) — AXELOS's framework for IT service management.
- ISO 31000 (risk acceptance) — ISO 31000:2018 Risk management — Guidelines.
- Decision record — A short, versioned record of a significant decision: its context, the options, the choice and its consequences.
- Go / No-Go review — The meeting where the named release decider reads each release criterion against its evidence and decides go, no-go, or go with conditions — and records it.
- A named person, a date, a decision — A release exists when an accountable person records go, no-go or go with conditions on a date — not when code reaches production.
- Evidence over assertion — A sentence is not evidence; every release criterion links to the artifact that proves it, for this build.
- Release readiness review — A structured check, before the Go / No-Go, that every release criterion has an owner and an artifact, so the meeting only decides.

Run this process end to end with me, one subprocess at a time, in this order:
- 6.1.1 Assemble the Release Candidate — gate: Scope Confirmed
    produces: Release candidate, Out-of-scope list, Dependency list
- 6.1.2 Raise & Approve the Change — gate: Change Approved
    produces: Change record, Change approval, Change calendar entry, Emergency change record
- 6.1.3 Write Release Notes — gate: Notes Approved
    produces: Release notes, Known issues list

    produces: Go / No-Go decision record, Release criteria evaluation, Conditions register

After each subprocess, summarise what we produced, list open questions and assumptions, and wait for my go-ahead. Use the separate subprocess prompts if we need more depth.
At the end, prepare the Go / No-Go review: check our evidence against the criteria below and recommend forward, rework or stop. I decide.

## Apply
- ITIL 4 (change enablement & release management) — AXELOS's framework for IT service management.
- ISO/IEC 20000-1 (change management) — ISO/IEC 20000-1:2018 Information technology — Service management — Part 1: Service management system requirements.
- Decision record — A short, versioned record of a significant decision: its context, the options, the choice and its consequences.
- Go / No-Go review — The meeting where the named release decider reads each release criterion against its evidence and decides go, no-go, or go with conditions — and records it.
- Peer review of changes — A change is reviewed by someone other than its author, at an authority level that matches its risk — the lightweight alternative to a weekly change board.
- A named person, a date, a decision — A release exists when an accountable person records go, no-go or go with conditions on a date — not when code reaches production.
- Exclude explicitly, with reasons — What is not in the release is written down with the reason, and the people who asked for it are told before deployment.
- Change risk assessment — Rates a change's likelihood of failure and its impact to choose its type, authority, window and safeguards.
- Release readiness review — A structured check, before the Go / No-Go, that every release criterion has an owner and an artifact, so the meeting only decides.

- Governance / Risk (required)
- DevOps / Delivery (required)
- Product (required)

- Concern: Unowned conditions
- Constraint: Change windows and freezes

- Scope is never conditional
- A go is the only thing that makes stories Released

## If it goes off the happy path
- Evidence is weak or work fails a check → No-go → the failing criterion returns to VERIFY, 6.1.1 or 6.2.2

- It should stop → No-go with no path → release cancelled; stories stay verified and unreleased; what must change and why — recorded in the learning log

## Output
- Release candidate — a document with these sections:
    - 1. Objective: What this release is for, in one sentence. Scope arguments are judged against it.
    - 2. Build: The exact build — version, commit, digest.
    - 3. In scope: Each picked story — verified against this build, with evidence.

    - 5. Dependencies: Migrations, flags, third parties, other teams — each with an owner and a state.

    - Not in this release: What people asked for but is excluded.

    - Help: Where to get help.

    - Decision: Go, no-go, or go with conditions.

    (example row: C1 | Lyon scan accuracy 91% vs 95% target | Ops manager | Engineering lead | Accuracy ≥ 95% on 200 Lyon PDFs, or review threshold raised to 95% confidence | 2025-07-02 | RING-2 Lyon | Open)

Context from me: $ARGUMENTS

I'm the devOps / platform engineer on {{initiative}}. I'm working on process 6.2: Deployment.
Goal: Promote the verified build to production automatically and reversibly, with exposure off, so deployment carries no user risk.
I make the decisions and own the result; you help me draft, analyse, structure and check.

## Context I'm attaching
- Release candidate
- Release build
- Go / No-Go decision record
- Runbook
- {{anything else relevant}}

## Before we start
Check these are true, or tell me what's missing:
- Release candidate assembled
- Release build in the registry

## What to do
Run this process end to end with me, one subprocess at a time, in this order:
- 6.2.1 Plan the Deployment & Rollback — gate: Deployment Plan Approved
    produces: Deployment plan, Rollback plan, Migration plan
- 6.2.2 Rehearse & Prove Rollback — gate: Rollback Proven
    produces: Staging rehearsal record, Deployment record
- 6.2.3 Deploy to Production — gate: Deployed
    produces: Deployment record, Smoke check results
- 6.2.4 Roll Back or Roll Forward — gate: Service Restored
    produces: Rollback record, Problem record
- In parallel: Planning and rehearsal run before the Go / No-Go
- In parallel: Rehearsal ∥ launch readiness
After each subprocess, summarise what we produced, list open questions and assumptions, and wait for my go-ahead. Use the separate subprocess prompts if we need more depth.
At the end, prepare the Deployed with Rollback Proven review: check our evidence against the criteria below and recommend forward, rework or stop. I decide.

## Apply
- ITIL 4 (deployment management) — AXELOS's framework for IT service management.
- Site Reliability Engineering — Google's discipline of running services with software-engineering methods: reliability is defined by SLOs, the gap to 100% is an error budget to spend on change, and toil is engineered away.
- ISO/IEC 20000-1 (release & deployment management) — ISO/IEC 20000-1:2018 Information technology — Service management — Part 1: Service management system requirements.
- ISO/IEC 27001 (A.8.31 separation of environments) — ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Information security management systems — Requirements.
- Build once, deploy many — Build one immutable artifact and promote that same artifact through every environment, so what was tested is exactly what runs.
- Expand / contract migration — Change a database in backward-compatible steps — expand (add), migrate, contract (remove) — so each deployment can be rolled back.
- Blue-green deployment — Run two identical production environments; deploy to the idle one, test it, then switch traffic — and switch back to roll back.
- Rollback rehearsal — Running the deployment and its rollback end to end in staging, with the release build, and timing both.
- Smoke testing — A short, automated set of checks run right after deployment that exercise the critical path end to end.
- Continuous integration & delivery — Developers integrate small changes to the main branch many times a day; an automated pipeline builds, tests and keeps the software releasable at all times.

## Keep in mind
- DevOps / Delivery (required)
- Infrastructure / Platform (required)
- Reliability / Resilience (required)
- Operations (required)
- Concern: Irreversible steps
- Concern: Drift between tested and deployed
- Constraint: Change window
- Constraint: Data migrations

## Rules
- No deployment without a recorded go and an approved change
- No manual changes in production
- Build once, deploy many
- Deploy outside business peaks

## If it goes off the happy path
- Evidence is weak or work fails a check → Rollback fails in staging → fix the plan; deployment fails → 6.2.4
- A different valid path appears → Blue-green → switch traffic, keep blue warm
- It goes beyond my authority → Unplanned impact → release manager; data damage → incident command
- It should stop → Release withdrawn → stories back to BUILD with a rollback record and a problem record — recorded in the learning log

## Output
- Deployment plan — a document with these sections:
    - Pre-checks: What must be true before the pipeline starts.
    - Steps: Pipeline stages in order, with expected duration.
    - Migrations: Expand / contract steps and how each is reversed.
    - Point of no return: Any step after which rollback means roll-forward.
    - Verification: How we know each step worked.
    - Communication: Who is told at start, end and on failure.
- Rollback plan — a document with these sections:
    - Triggers: The conditions that start a rollback — written before deployment.
    - Fastest path: The quickest safe undo.
    - Full rollback: Redeploy the previous version.
    - Data and migrations: Expand / contract steps; what is reversible.
    - One-way doors: Anything that cannot be undone — named explicitly.
    - Decision and owner: Who decides to roll back during the window and after.
- Staging rehearsal record — fill these fields: Build; Deployed to staging; Deploy time; Rollback exercised (Flag off / Redeploy previous / Both); Rollback time; Data checked after rollback; Issues found; Pipeline run; Rehearsed by
- Deployment record — a table with columns: DEP ID | Release | Change | Build / digest | Environment | Started | Finished | Pipeline run | Result | Flags at end
    (example row: DEP-0029 | RC-014 | — | 2.3.0-rc2 · 7c1e… | Staging | 2025-06-20 10:02 | 2025-06-20 10:13 | #1879 | Succeeded | All on)

- Kill switch — An operational toggle that turns a capability off instantly, without a deployment, when it misbehaves.

- Feature-flag service — Manages runtime flags and their targeting, with an audit log.

- AI / ML: Is the parser drifting on this site's scans?
- DevOps / Delivery: A configuration fix is still a logged change.

- Rework: Fix didn't hold → stay paused and diagnose again

## If it goes off the happy path
- Pause → diagnose, fix, resume
- Rollback threshold → recover
- Noise → confirm and continue

- S2. ◆ DECISION — Operations accepts? (Operations lead)  [if: Rejected → fill the gaps; Disputed acceptance → sponsor]

- Operational acceptance — Operations formally accepts a service into live running once it has what it needs to run it: runbook, monitoring, alerts, SLOs, support model, known errors.
- Guardrail metrics (become alerts) — Defines the metrics that must not degrade during a rollout, each with a baseline, a pause threshold and a rollback threshold, captured before enablement.
- Decide explicitly — Every gate ends in a named decision with an owner and a rationale — never by default.
- Feature toggles (flag removal) — A switch in the code, controlled at run time, that turns a capability on or off for chosen users — separating deploying code from releasing it.
- Backlog tool — Holds the portfolio, product and iteration backlogs as linked items so every story traces up to its initiative.
- Release record system — The system of record for releases: picks, owners, evidence links, the decision, the production check and the close.
- Release checklist — A short, ordered checklist for the release window — pre-checks, steps, verification, communication.
- ISO/IEC 20000-1 (post-implementation review) — ISO/IEC 20000-1:2018 Information technology — Service management — Part 1: Service management system requirements.
- DORA metrics — The DevOps Research and Assessment measures of software delivery performance: deployment frequency, lead time for changes, change failure rate and time to restore service (with reliability).
- Retrospective — A structured, blameless look back at a piece of work to decide what to keep, stop and change — held for every outcome, including kills.

- Operations: Runbook, SLOs, alerts and known errors in the pack.
- Security: Access and secrets handed over cleanly.
- Operations: Operations lead accepts in writing.
- Support / Service Mgmt: Support model after hypercare agreed.
- Product: Flag removal ranked in the product backlog.
- Governance / Risk: Change and release closed with the outcome.
- Compliance / Regulatory: Record complete for audit.
- Reliability / Resilience: SLOs live and owned by OPERATE.

## Rules
- Rework: Rejected handover → fill the gaps and re-present

## If it goes off the happy path
- Accepted → close and hand over
- Rejected → fill gaps
- Disputed → sponsor

- Operational handover pack — a pack with: Runbook, SLO targets & dashboards, Guardrail metrics, Post-deployment verification report, Known errors, Support enablement pack, Service acceptance
- Release record — a pack with: Release candidate, Change record, Go / No-Go decision record, Deployment record, Ring record, Post-deployment verification report, Close

## What to do

- 6.5.1 Run Smoke Checks — gate: Smoke Passed
    produces: Smoke check results, Synthetic check results
- 6.5.2 Verify Production Against Predictions — gate: Production Verified

- 6.5.3 Run Hypercare — gate: Hypercare Exit

## Apply
- Site Reliability Engineering — Google's discipline of running services with software-engineering methods: reliability is defined by SLOs, the gap to 100% is an error budget to spend on change, and toil is engineered away.
- DORA metrics — The DevOps Research and Assessment measures of software delivery performance: deployment frequency, lead time for changes, change failure rate and time to restore service (with reliability).
- ISO/IEC 20000-1 (monitoring release success) — ISO/IEC 20000-1:2018 Information technology — Service management — Part 1: Service management system requirements.
- ISO/IEC 25010 (quality in use) — ISO/IEC 25010:2023 Systems and software Quality Requirements and Evaluation (SQuaRE) — Product quality model.
- Dark launch — Deploy new code to production with users unexposed — exercising it with internal or shadow traffic before anyone depends on it.
- Smoke testing — A short, automated set of checks run right after deployment that exercise the critical path end to end.
- Production verification — Checking production against the things the release said would be true — NFRs, guardrails, success metrics and the consequences recorded in decisions — not just 'no errors'.
- Hypercare — A short, defined period after launch with extra support, daily check-ins and the building team on hand.
- Operational acceptance — Operations formally accepts a service into live running once it has what it needs to run it: runbook, monitoring, alerts, SLOs, support model, known errors.

Load these skills if you can: build-once-deploy-many, continuous-integration-and-delivery, release-readiness-review, semantic-versioning, change-risk-assessment, risk-matrix, peer-review-of-changes, single-accountable-owner (+33 more).
Run it as specified in `workflows/release-act.md`, stopping at every checkpoint.
Context from me: $ARGUMENTS

I'm the engineering lead, DevOps / platform engineer, Support lead on {{initiative}}. Help me run this act end to end.
Goal: Move verified change into production safely and reversibly, on a recorded decision, with the people who use and support it ready.
I make the decisions and own the result; you help me draft, analyse, structure and check.

## Context I'm attaching
- Quality gate record
- Verified increments
- Release build
- Runbook
- {{anything else relevant}}

## Before we start
Check these are true, or tell me what's missing:
- Quality gate record (VERIFY) passed or conditionally passed
- Verified increments against a named build
- Runbook and release build from BUILD

## What to do
Run this act end to end with me, one process at a time, in this order:
- 6.1 Release Prep & Change Approval — gate: Go / No-Go
    produces: Release candidate, Change record, Release notes, Go / No-Go decision record, Conditions register
- 6.2 Deployment — gate: Deployed with Rollback Proven
    produces: Deployment plan, Rollback plan, Staging rehearsal record, Deployment record, Rollback record
- 6.3 Progressive Rollout — gate: Full Exposure
    produces: Exposure plan, Guardrail definitions, Ring record, Flag change log
- 6.4 Launch Readiness — gate: Launch Readiness
    produces: Support enablement pack, Communications plan, User documentation, Training record, Launch readiness record
- 6.5 Post-Deployment Verification — gate: Release Closed
    produces: Smoke check results, Post-deployment verification report, Hypercare log, Operational handover pack, Release record, Release retrospective, Learning log
- In parallel: 6.4 runs alongside 6.1 — launch readiness is a Go / No-Go input
- In parallel: Deployment planning and rehearsal (6.2.1–6.2.2) and the exposure plan (6.3.1) run before the go
- In parallel: Hypercare (6.5.3) overlaps the later rings
After each process, summarise what we produced, list open questions and assumptions, and wait for my go-ahead. Use the separate process prompts if we need more depth.
At the end, prepare the Go / No-Go review: check our evidence against the criteria below and recommend forward, rework or stop. I decide.

## Apply
- ITIL 4 — AXELOS's framework for IT service management.
- Site Reliability Engineering — Google's discipline of running services with software-engineering methods: reliability is defined by SLOs, the gap to 100% is an error budget to spend on change, and toil is engineered away.
- Progressive delivery — Releasing to users in controlled steps — flags, rings, canaries — while watching guardrails, so exposure grows only as evidence of health grows.
- ISO/IEC 20000-1 (change, release & deployment) — ISO/IEC 20000-1:2018 Information technology — Service management — Part 1: Service management system requirements.
- ISO/IEC 27001 (change management) — ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Information security management systems — Requirements.
- Feature toggles — A switch in the code, controlled at run time, that turns a capability on or off for chosen users — separating deploying code from releasing it.
- Ring deployment — Expose a change in concentric rings of users — from the team, to pilot users, to one site, to everyone — each ring a small go / no-go.
- Canary release — Expose the new version to a small, representative slice of users or traffic first, compare it with the rest, and only then widen.
- Go / No-Go review — The meeting where the named release decider reads each release criterion against its evidence and decides go, no-go, or go with conditions — and records it.
- Continuous integration & delivery — Developers integrate small changes to the main branch many times a day; an automated pipeline builds, tests and keeps the software releasable at all times.

## Keep in mind
- DevOps / Delivery (required)
- Operations (required)
- Reliability / Resilience (required)
- Support / Service Mgmt (required)
- Concern: Big-bang exposure
- Concern: Unproven rollback
- Concern: Users and support caught unprepared
- Constraint: Change windows and freezes
- Constraint: Decision rights

## Rules
- A go — named person, date, outcome — is the only thing that makes stories Released
- Scope (only verified stories) is never conditional
- Every condition has an owner, evidence and a due date
- Every rollback raises a problem record; every release, including a rolled-back one, ends with a retrospective
- Change management per ISO/IEC 20000-1
- No exposure before support, comms, docs and training are ready

## If it goes off the happy path
- Evidence is weak or work fails a check → Guardrail breach → roll back (6.2.4); no-go → back to VERIFY, BUILD or 6.1.1 as the failing criterion says
- A different valid path appears → Pause at the current ring; conditions hold the rings they block
- It goes beyond my authority → Go / No-Go dispute → sponsor as release authority; severity breach → incident command
- It should stop → No-go with no path or kill switch → release cancelled or withdrawn; stories return unreleased with the reason; recorded in the learning log

## Output
- Release candidate — a document with these sections:
    - 1. Objective: What this release is for, in one sentence. Scope arguments are judged against it.
    - 2. Build: The exact build — version, commit, digest.
    - 3. In scope: Each picked story — verified against this build, with evidence.
    - 4. Out of scope: Everything excluded, with the reason, and who was told.
    - 5. Dependencies: Migrations, flags, third parties, other teams — each with an owner and a state.
    - 6. Gate conditions and owners: Each Go / No-Go condition with its owner.
- Change record — fill these fields: Change ID; Release; Type (Standard (pre-approved) / Normal / Emergency); What changes; Services and users affected; Risk (likelihood × impact); Main risks; Window; Rollback plan; Change authority; Approved; Closed with outcome (Successful / Successful with issues / Failed / Rolled back)
- Go / No-Go decision record — a document with these sections:
    - Decision: Go, no-go, or go with conditions.
    - Criteria: Link to the evaluation; which were not met.
    - Conditions: Each unmet criterion: accepted by, owner, evidence, due date, what it blocks.
    - Rationale: Why this decision, citing the evidence.
    - On no-go: what must change: The failing criterion and where work returns.
    - Next step: Deploy and rollout per the plans.
    - Decision: Go / Go with conditions / No-go
- Deployment record — a table with columns: DEP ID | Release | Change | Build / digest | Environment | Started | Finished | Pipeline run | Result | Flags at end
    (example row: DEP-0029 | RC-014 | — | 2.3.0-rc2 · 7c1e… | Staging | 2025-06-20 10:02 | 2025-06-20 10:13 | #1879 | Succeeded | All on)
- Ring record — fill these fields: Ring; Exposed from / to; Users / orders; Guardrail readings; Breaches; User feedback; Decision (Promote / Hold / Pause / Roll back); Decided by; Date
- Launch readiness record — fill these fields: Release; Support enabled (briefing, KB, escalation, hypercare); Communications approved and scheduled; User docs published, localised and accessible; Training done for the next ring; Runbook updated and handed to on-call; Gaps and their owners; Ready for (All rings / Next ring only / Not ready); Confirmed by
- Release notes — a document with these sections:
    - What's new: Each change in the reader's words, linked to its story.
    - What you do differently: The changed task, in one or two lines.
    - Known issues: Open defects and accepted risks that readers will notice, with the workaround.
    - Not in this release: What people asked for but is excluded.
    - Rollout: Who gets it when.
    - Help: Where to get help.
- Post-deployment verification report — a document with these sections:
    - Claim vs evidence: Each prediction and what production shows.
    - Guardrails through the rings: Readings per ring, breaches and what was done.
    - Success metrics: Early readings of the outcome — not the outcome review.
    - Soak: How long at full exposure, and what happened.
    - Issues found: Defects and problems raised.
    - Result: Passed / passed with issues / failed.
    - Decision: Passed / Passed with issues / Failed
- Release record — a pack with: Release candidate, Change record, Go / No-Go decision record, Deployment record, Ring record, Post-deployment verification report, Close
- Learning log — a table with columns: Learning ID | Date | From (unit / decision) | What happened | What we learned | Change we'll make | Type | Owner | Applied?
    (example row: LRN-007 | 2025-04-02 | DEC-012 · Discovery Decision | Go with condition on vendor connector | Vendor dependency surfaced late (1.5) — should be scanned in 1.4 | Add vendor-support check to Existing Solutions scan | Retrospective | Product manager | ☐)

## Before you finish, check
- [ ] Every in-scope story verified against the release build
- [ ] No open Sev-1/2 defects
- [ ] Non-functional criteria demonstrated
- [ ] Rollback exercised in staging
- [ ] Success metrics emitting before enablement
- [ ] Out-of-scope list agreed
- [ ] Change approved
- [ ] Launch readiness confirmed
- [ ] Go / No-Go recorded by the named decider
- [ ] Release deployed, rolled out and verified in production
- [ ] Release closed with its outcome; service accepted by OPERATE

## Ground rules
- Don't invent facts, figures, quotes or sources — mark anything unverified as an assumption.
- If something you need is missing, ask me instead of guessing.
- Keep personal or confidential data out unless I've provided it for this purpose.
- Prepare decisions; don't make them — I decide.

files.title: Guardrails & hooks
files.body:
# Guardrails & hooks — Release

People own the work, agents help do it. In every unit the person in the role briefs the agent, gives it the right context, checks what it produces, and makes every decision. The agent drafts, researches, analyses, structures and checks — it never decides, approves or signs.

## Always
- Don't invent facts, figures, quotes or sources — mark anything unverified as an assumption.
- If something you need is missing, ask me instead of guessing.
- Keep personal or confidential data out unless I've provided it for this purpose.
- Prepare decisions; don't make them — I decide.
- Never paste passwords, keys, or personal data you aren't allowed to share — anonymise first
- At enterprise scale, use only approved tools
- Check every fact, number and source the agent gives you
- Agents prepare decisions; people make them
- Save the output in the artifact template and note that an agent helped
- If the agent's output is wrong, correct the prompt or the context — then record what you learned

## Scale: Solo / small
- Read and write everything in the project folder; you review before anything is shared.
- Watch for: Skipping discovery because 'I already know'
- Watch for: Accepting agent output unreviewed because there's no one else to check it

## Hooks — automatic where your agent supports them, a checklist everywhere else
| When | Check | If it fails |
|---|---|---|
| Before saving an artifact | It follows its template · it carries its trace ID and links upstream IDs · every claim cites evidence or is marked 'Assumption:' · no personal data or secrets | Fix, or stop and tell me |
| Before a decision step | Stop. Prepare the decision brief. Wait for the named decision-maker | Never decide or approve |
| Before anything leaves the team | Messages, posts, invitations and shared documents are drafts until a person sends them | Ask for approval |
| Before using a new tool or data source | Is it allowed at this scale? Is the data allowed in this tool? | Ask first |
| After each step | Append to PROGRESS.md: date, unit, what was done, artifacts, decisions, open questions, next | Always |

## Rules and policies by unit
### RELEASE
- A go — named person, date, outcome — is the only thing that makes stories Released
- Scope (only verified stories) is never conditional
- Every condition has an owner, evidence and a due date
- Every rollback raises a problem record; every release, including a rolled-back one, ends with a retrospective
- Change management per ISO/IEC 20000-1
- No exposure before support, comms, docs and training are ready
- Change windows and freezes
- Decision rights

### 6.1 Release Prep & Change Approval
- Scope is never conditional
- A go is the only thing that makes stories Released
- Change policy per ISO/IEC 20000-1
- Decider named before the release
- Change windows and freezes

### 6.1.1 Assemble the Release Candidate
- A story cannot be in two open releases
- Scope — only verified stories — is never conditional
- Requesters of excluded work are told before deployment
- Only verified stories
- The release window

### 6.1.2 Raise & Approve the Change
- No production change without an approved change record
- Emergency changes reviewed within two working days
- Change policy per ISO/IEC 20000-1
- Security review for new data flows
- Change freezes
- Business peak hours

### 6.1.3 Write Release Notes
- Never describe what is not in the build
- Plain language, written for each audience
- Release scope

### 6.1.4 Hold the Go / No-Go Decision
- Scope — only verified stories — is never conditional
- A go is the only thing that makes stories Released
- A no-go names what must change
- The decider is named before the release, not during it
- Release window
- Decision rights

### 6.2 Deployment
- No deployment without a recorded go and an approved change
- No manual changes in production
- Build once, deploy many
- Deploy outside business peaks
- Change window
- Data migrations

### 6.2.1 Plan the Deployment & Rollback
- No manual changes in production
- No contract migration in the same release as its expand
- Build once, deploy many
- Window length
- Data migrations

### 6.2.2 Rehearse & Prove Rollback
- An unrehearsed rollback fails the Go / No-Go
- Rehearse every release, not only the 'big' ones
- Staging parity

### 6.2.3 Deploy to Production
- No deployment without a recorded go and an approved change
- No hand edits in production
- Deploy outside business peaks
- Change window

### 6.2.4 Roll Back or Roll Forward
- Roll back first, diagnose later
- A roll-forward is a new change with its own go
- Every rollback raises a problem record
- Time to restore

### 6.3 Progressive Rollout
- Thresholds set before exposure and never moved after
- One ring at a time
- Every release flag has an owner and a removal date
- Site freezes
- Open conditions

### 6.3.1 Configure Flags & Exposure Plan
- Thresholds are set before exposure and never moved after
- Every release flag has an owner and a removal date
- Site freezes
- Flag capability in the build

### 6.3.2 Run Ring 0 (Canary)
- Never promote on a breached threshold
- Ring 0 users are trained and know how to report
- Soak time
- Pilot volume

### 6.3.3 Promote Through the Rings
- One ring at a time
- No promotion inside a freeze
- Users told and trained before their ring
- Freezes
- Open conditions

### 6.3.4 Watch Guardrails, Pause or Roll Back
- Rollback threshold breached → roll back, no debate
- Every pause and resume logged
- Pre-agreed thresholds

### 6.4 Launch Readiness
- No ring enabled for untrained or unsupported users
- Localised for every site in scope
- WCAG 2.2 AA for user documentation
- Translation lead time
- Shift patterns

### 6.4.1 Enable Support
- No exposure before support is briefed
- Hypercare length and exit criteria set in advance
- Support capacity

### 6.4.2 Plan & Send Launch Communications
- Never announce a date a ring hasn't confirmed
- Localised for each site
- Ring dates

### 6.4.3 Publish User & Operational Documentation
- Docs versioned with the release
- Localised for every site in scope
- Translation lead time

### 6.4.4 Train Users & Confirm Readiness
- No ring enabled for untrained users
- Readiness is confirmed per ring, not once
- Shift patterns
- Languages

### 6.5 Post-Deployment Verification
- No release closed without a production check
- Mismatches become defects, problems or ADR updates
- Every release gets a retrospective
- Flags removed on a scheduled date
- Soak length
- Operations acceptance criteria

### 6.5.1 Run Smoke Checks
- No exposure before smoke passes
- Smoke never uses real customer data
- Synthetic checks stay on after the release
- No real data in smoke

### 6.5.2 Verify Production Against Predictions
- A release is not closed without a production check
- Claims cite numbers, not adjectives
- Mismatches become defects, problems or ADR updates — never notes
- Soak length
- Measurement maturity

### 6.5.3 Run Hypercare
- Every defect routed to the backlog with severity and owner
- The building team stays on hand during hypercare
- Team availability

### 6.5.4 Close the Release & Hand Over to OPERATE
- Closed only after the production check and soak
- Change record closed with its outcome
- Every release gets a retrospective
- Operations acceptance criteria

files.title: How to use this kit
files.body:
# Node agent kit — Release

A ready project folder for running this act with your agent. People drive, decide and sign off; agents help.

## What's inside
- **Context file** — `AGENTS.md`: What the agent always knows about the initiative: how we work, the lifecycle, conventions, trace IDs, templates, ground rules and scale.
- **Skills** — `skills/<name>/SKILL.md`: Reusable how-to packages — one per technique or method — with steps, structure, output templates and checks. The agent loads one when the task needs it.
- **Commands** — `commands/<name>.md`: Saved prompts you run by name, with arguments — one per step, workflow, subprocess, process and the act.
- **Workflows** — `workflows/<name>.md`: A run specification: steps in order, inputs and outputs as files, who owns each step, human checkpoints, decision branches, recovery and the gate.
- **Subagents** — `agents/<name>.md`: Specialised helpers with one job — lens reviewers (privacy, security, finance…), a researcher, a synthesiser, a challenger, a decision-brief writer.
- **Tools & connectors** — `TOOLS.md`: Which tools and data each step needs — web search, documents, spreadsheets, the backlog tool, the research repository, the code repository — and what each scale allows the agent to do with them.
- **Guardrails & hooks** — `GUARDRAILS.md`: Rules the agent must follow and automatic checks at key moments — before saving an artifact, before a decision, before sending anything outside the team.
- **Rubrics** — `rubrics/<artifact>.md`: A scored checklist for each artifact, from its template, quality criteria and the unit's criteria.
- **Memory & handoff** — `PROGRESS.md · TRACE.md · docs/`: What carries across sessions and people: the project folder, a progress log, and a trace-ID register.
- **Templates** — `templates/`: the artifact templates the work produces.

## Set it up
1. Put this folder at the root of your project repository or shared drive and fill `{{initiative}}` in AGENTS.md.
2. Point your agent at it — how each layer is picked up:
   - Context file: Many coding agents read AGENTS.md at the repository root. Tools with their own file (e.g. CLAUDE.md) can import or copy it. In chat assistants, paste it into the project's instructions.
   - Skills: Agents that support skills load SKILL.md folders from their skills directory. Otherwise attach the SKILL.md as a file, or paste it before the prompt.
   - Commands: Agents with custom commands or saved prompts read Markdown files from their commands / prompts folder; $ARGUMENTS takes what you type after the name. Otherwise paste the file.
   - Workflows: Point the agent at the workflow file ("run workflows/x.md, stop at every checkpoint"). Orchestration tools can execute the YAML block; people can read it as a checklist.
   - Subagents: Agents that support subagents load them from their agents folder. Otherwise open a separate conversation and paste the file as its first message.
   - Tools & connectors: Connect tools through your agent's connectors or MCP servers; grant the least access the step needs.
   - Guardrails & hooks: Agents with hooks can run these checks automatically; everywhere else they're a checklist the agent applies and you confirm.
   - Rubrics: Any agent: "score docs/x.md against rubrics/x.md".
   - Memory & handoff: Keep them in the repository or shared drive the agent can read; start each session with "read PROGRESS.md".
3. Start with the command `release-run-act`, or the command for the unit you're on.
4. After every step: check the output, score it against its rubric, save it in `docs/`, and log it in PROGRESS.md.

Tools change quickly — check your agent's documentation for where it reads context files, skills, commands and subagents.

files.body:

Use when services that need near-instant rollback of the whole version. In Node: 6.2.1.1 S2 Design migrations expand / contract; 6.2.4.1 S2 Flag off or redeploy previous."

# Blue-green deployment

_Pattern_ — Run two identical production environments; deploy to the idle one, test it, then switch traffic — and switch back to roll back.

## When to use it
Services that need near-instant rollback of the whole version.

Applied in Node at:
- 6.2.1.1 S2 Design migrations expand / contract — command `release-6-2-1-1-s2-design-migrations-expand-contract`
- 6.2.4.1 S2 Flag off or redeploy previous — command `release-6-2-4-1-s2-flag-off-or-redeploy-previous`

## How to do it
1. Deploy to the idle (green) environment
2. Verify it
3. Switch the router to green
4. Keep blue warm for instant rollback

## Structure
1. Blue live
2. Deploy to green
3. Verify green
4. Switch traffic
5. Blue kept for rollback

## Output
Write results with these templates:
- Migration plan → `templates/migration-plan.md`, saved as `docs/migration-plan.md`
- Flag change log → `templates/flag-log.md`, saved as `docs/flag-log.md`

- Avoid: Database changes that only one colour can read
- Migration plan: Each step reversible
- Migration plan: Verification query defined
- Migration plan: Rehearsed before production
- Flag change log: Every change has a reason and a decision
- Flag change log: Removal date set for the flag
- Every claim cites evidence or is marked "Assumption:"

Jez Humble & David Farley, Continuous Delivery (2010)

# Build once, deploy many

_Pattern_ — Build one immutable artifact and promote that same artifact through every environment, so what was tested is exactly what runs.

## When to use it
Every deployment.

Applied in Node at:
- 6.1.1.1 S2 Pick verified stories — command `release-6-1-1-1-s2-pick-verified-stories`
- 6.2.1.1 S1 List pipeline steps & timings — command `release-6-2-1-1-s1-list-pipeline-steps-and-timings`

- 6.2.3.1 S2 Run pipeline: migrate & deploy — command `release-6-2-3-1-s2-run-pipeline-migrate-and-deploy`

## How to do it
1. Build once in the pipeline
2. Store by digest in the artifact registry
3. Promote the same digest to staging, then production
4. Keep configuration outside the artifact

## Structure
1. Build
2. Registry (digest)
3. Staging
4. Production

## Output
Write results with these templates:
- Release scope → `templates/release-candidate.md`, saved as `docs/release-candidate.md`

- Avoid: Rebuilding for production 'with the fix'

- Release scope: Every exclusion has a reason
- Release scope: Every dependency has an owner and a state
- Deployment plan: Fully automated
- Deployment plan: Same steps as staging

- Deployment record: Recorded by the pipeline, not by hand

Humble & Farley, Continuous Delivery

## When to use it
Every normal or emergency change.

Applied in Node at:

# Go / No-Go review

_Practice_ — The meeting where the named release decider reads each release criterion against its evidence and decides go, no-go, or go with conditions — and records it.

## When to use it
Every release.

Applied in Node at:
- 6.1.4.1 S2 Circulate the pack — command `release-6-1-4-1-s2-circulate-the-pack`

## How to do it
1. Circulate the pack 24 hours before
2. Walk each criterion: met or not, with the artifact
3. For each unmet criterion: no-go, or a condition with an owner, evidence and date
4. Decide — a named person, a date, the outcome
5. Record and communicate

## Structure
| Outcome | When | What must be recorded |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Go | Every criterion met | Decider, date, criteria results |
| Go with conditions | Some unmet, risk accepted | Each condition: accepted by, owner, evidence, due date, what it blocks |
| No-go | Unacceptable gap | What failed, what must change, where work returns |

## Output
Write results with these templates:
- Go / No-Go pack → `templates/go-no-go-pack.md`, saved as `docs/go-no-go-pack.md`

## Quality checks
- Avoid: Deciding in the room on evidence nobody has read
- Avoid: 'Broadly yes' instead of yes or no
- Avoid: Conditions without owners
- Go / No-Go pack: Circulated 24 h before the meeting
- Go / No-Go pack: Every criterion has evidence
- Every claim cites evidence or is marked "Assumption:"

## Source
Delivery manual — The Release Gate; ITIL 4 release management

---

# ITIL 4

_Framework_ — AXELOS's framework for IT service management. Its service value system links demand to value through governance, practices and continual improvement, and covers services from design to retirement.

## When to use it
Continual improvement of running services, service portfolio decisions and service retirement.

Applied in Node at:
- 6.1.2.2 S1 Raise the emergency change (applied as: change enablement) — command `release-6-1-2-2-s1-raise-the-emergency-change`

## How to do it
1. Start from the value the service co-creates with its consumers
2. Run the service value chain: plan, improve, engage, design & transition, obtain / build, deliver & support
3. Apply the continual improvement model to every service
4. Retire services deliberately through service configuration and portfolio management

## Structure
1. **What is the vision?** — Business goals
2. **Where are we now?** — Baseline assessment
3. **Where do we want to be?** — Measurable targets
4. **How do we get there?** — Improvement plan
5. **Take action** — Execute the plan
6. **Did we get there?** — Measurements and KPIs
7. **How do we keep the momentum going?** — Embed and repeat
→ then repeat

## Output
Write results with these templates:
- Emergency change record → `templates/change-record.md`, saved as `docs/change-record.md`

## Quality checks
- Avoid: Adopting every practice as a heavy process
- Avoid: Improvement registers no one prioritises
- Emergency change record: Type and authority match the risk
- Emergency change record: Window avoids business peaks and freezes
- Emergency change record: Rollback linked
- Every claim cites evidence or is marked "Assumption:"

## Source
AXELOS, ITIL 4 Foundation (2019)

# Retrospective

_Practice_ — A structured, blameless look back at a piece of work to decide what to keep, stop and change — held for every outcome, including kills.

## When to use it
At the end of discovery, whatever the decision, and after any stop.

Applied in Node at:

## How to do it
1. Set the scene: purpose, blameless rules
2. Gather data: timeline, what went well, what didn't, surprises
3. Generate insights: why did it happen?
4. Decide changes — each with an owner
5. Record in the learning log and close

## Structure
| Keep doing | Stop / change | Surprises | Changes (owner) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
|  |  |  |  |

- Avoid: Changes without owners

files.body:
---
name: site-reliability-engineering
description: "Google's discipline of running services with software-engineering methods: reliability is defined by SLOs, the gap to 100% is an error budget to spend on change, and toil is engineered away. Use when any service people depend on — scaled down for small teams, never skipped. In Node: 6.2.2.1 S5 Rollback worked within the window?; 6.3.4.2 S4 Restore exposure later, or withdraw?; 6.5.1.1 S4 Start synthetic checks."
---

# Site Reliability Engineering

_Framework_ — Google's discipline of running services with software-engineering methods: reliability is defined by SLOs, the gap to 100% is an error budget to spend on change, and toil is engineered away.

## When to use it
Any service people depend on — scaled down for small teams, never skipped.

Applied in Node at:
- 6.2.2.1 S5 Rollback worked within the window? — command `release-6-2-2-1-d1-rollback-worked-within-the-window`
- 6.3.4.2 S4 Restore exposure later, or withdraw? — command `release-6-3-4-2-d1-restore-exposure-later-or-withdraw`
- 6.5.1.1 S4 Start synthetic checks — command `release-6-5-1-1-s3-start-synthetic-checks`

## How to do it
1. Define SLIs from what users experience
2. Set SLOs below 100% and agree an error-budget policy
3. Alert on budget burn, not on causes
4. Respond to incidents with clear command and blameless postmortems
5. Cap toil and plan capacity ahead of demand

## Structure
| Practice | What it gives you |
| --- | --- |
| SLIs & SLOs | A shared, numeric definition of 'reliable enough' |
| Error budgets | A rule for choosing between shipping and fixing |
| Monitoring & alerting | Pages only for user-visible burn |
| Emergency response & postmortems | Fast restore and learning without blame |
| Capacity planning | Demand met with headroom |
| Toil reduction | Time for engineering, not repetition |

## Output
Write results with these templates:
- Synthetic check results → `templates/smoke-results.md`, saved as `docs/smoke-results.md`

## Quality checks
- Avoid: Copying Google's tooling instead of its practices
- Avoid: SLOs set at 100%
- Avoid: An 'SRE team' that just does operations
- Synthetic check results: Run automatically by the pipeline
- Synthetic check results: Exercise the real path, not just a health check
- Every claim cites evidence or is marked "Assumption:"

## Source
Beyer et al., Site Reliability Engineering (2016) and The Site Reliability Workbook (2018)

## Timeline
_Key moments from assembly to close._
> Example: Assembled 18 June → Go with conditions 24 June → Lyon paused 2 July → closed 11 July.

_Keep doing._
> Example: Rollback rehearsed and timed; pilot clerks caught the review-screen wording early.

files.title: Rollback plan
files.body:
# Rollback plan — RC-014

- **Initiative:** 
- **Owner:** 
- **Version:** 
- **Status: Draft / In review / Approved:** 
- **Last updated:** 

## Triggers
_The conditions that start a rollback — written before deployment._
> Example: Smoke fails; parse accuracy < 90% for 30 min; order error rate above the 3% baseline; ERP import failures > 0.5%.


## Fastest path
_The quickest safe undo._
> Example: Site flag pdf-autofill off → clerks back to manual entry within 1 minute.


## Full rollback
_Redeploy the previous version._
> Example: Pipeline redeploys 2.2.4 (digest sha256:51ad…); ≈ 6 minutes; rehearsed in staging 20 June.


## Data and migrations
_Expand / contract steps; what is reversible._
> Example: parsed_order_lines added (expand) — harmless to 2.2.4; contract step deferred to 2.4.


## One-way doors
_Anything that cannot be undone — named explicitly._
> Example: Orders already pushed to the ERP stay; each is tagged source=autofill so they can be reviewed.


## Decision and owner
_Who decides to roll back during the window and after._
> Example: Release manager in the window; on-call engineer may flag off at any time without asking.

- Engineering lead: ____________  Date: ______
- Release manager: ____________  Date: ______

files.title: Workflow 6.1.1.1 · Assemble the Release Candidate
files.body:
# Workflow 6.1.1.1 · Assemble the Release Candidate

Assemble the release story by story from verified increments, with an objective, explicit exclusions and owners for every dependency and gate condition.

**Run it:** ask your agent to "run `workflows/release-6-1-1-1-assemble-rc.md` for {{initiative}}, stopping at every checkpoint", or use the command `release-6-1-1-1-run-assemble-rc`. Each checkpoint means: show me the output and wait. At `decision` checkpoints the named person decides.

```yaml
workflow: release-6-1-1-1-assemble-rc
title: "Assemble the Release Candidate"
owner: "Release manager"
inputs:
  - "docs/quality-gate-record.md"
  - "docs/verified-increment.md"
  - "docs/build-artifact.md"
preconditions:
  - "Quality gate passed or conditionally passed"
  - "Release build in the registry"
steps:
  - id: s1
    do: "Write the release objective"
    owner: "Release manager"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: release-6-1-1-1-s1-write-the-release-objective
    reviewers: [product-reviewer]
    output: "docs/release-candidate.md"
    checkpoint: review-at-end
  - id: s2
    do: "Pick verified stories"
    owner: "Release manager"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: release-6-1-1-1-s2-pick-verified-stories
    skills: [build-once-deploy-many]
    reviewers: [devops-reviewer, customer-reviewer]
    output: "docs/release-candidate.md"
    checkpoint: review-at-end
    on:
      "Nothing worth releasing": stop
  - id: d1
    decision: "Verified against the release build?"
    owner: "QA lead"
    agent: "prepare a decision brief — never decide"
    checkpoint: decision   # stop; QA lead decides
    branches:
      "yes": s3
      "Wrong build → re-verify or drop": s2
  - id: s3
    do: "Confirm dependencies & owners"
    owner: "Release manager"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: release-6-1-1-1-s3-confirm-dependencies-and-owners
    skills: [release-readiness-review]
    reviewers: [vendor-reviewer]
    output: "docs/release-candidate.md"
    checkpoint: review-at-end
  - id: s4
    do: "Agree the out-of-scope list"
    owner: "Product owner"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: release-6-1-1-1-s4-agree-the-out-of-scope-list
    reviewers: [product-reviewer, challenger]
    output: "docs/release-candidate.md"
    checkpoint: review-at-end
    on:
      "Disputed exclusion → product owner": authority
  - id: s5
    do: "Give each gate condition an owner"
    owner: "Release manager"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: release-6-1-1-1-s5-give-each-gate-condition-an-owner
    skills: [semantic-versioning]
    reviewers: [devops-reviewer]
    output: "docs/release-candidate.md"
    checkpoint: review-at-end
gate: "Scope Confirmed"
criteria:
  - "Only verified stories"
```

files.body:
# Workflow 6.1.2.1 · Raise & Approve the Change

Raise the change for the release, assess impact and risk, book a clear window and get it approved by an authority who is not its author.

**Run it:** ask your agent to "run `workflows/release-6-1-2-1-change.md` for {{initiative}}, stopping at every checkpoint", or use the command `release-6-1-2-1-run-change`. Each checkpoint means: show me the output and wait. At `decision` checkpoints the named person decides.

```yaml
workflow: release-6-1-2-1-change
title: "Raise & Approve the Change"
owner: "Release manager"
inputs:
  - "docs/release-candidate.md"
  - "docs/rollback-plan.md"
preconditions:
  - "Scope confirmed"
  - "Rollback plan drafted"
steps:
  - id: s1
    do: "Raise the change record"
    owner: "Release manager"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: release-6-1-2-1-s1-raise-the-change-record
    reviewers: [governance-reviewer, devops-reviewer]
    output: "docs/change-record.md"
    checkpoint: review-at-end
  - id: s2
    do: "Assess impact & risk"
    owner: "Release manager"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: release-6-1-2-1-s2-assess-impact-and-risk
    skills: [change-risk-assessment, risk-matrix]
    reviewers: [security-reviewer, infrastructure-reviewer, operations-reviewer]
    output: "docs/change-record.md"
    checkpoint: review-at-end
  - id: s3
    do: "Book the window"
    owner: "Release manager"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: release-6-1-2-1-s3-book-the-window
    reviewers: [operations-reviewer, compliance-reviewer]
    output: "docs/change-calendar.md"
    checkpoint: review-at-end
  - id: d1
    decision: "Approve?"
    owner: "Change authority"
    agent: "prepare a decision brief — never decide"
    checkpoint: decision   # stop; Change authority decides
    branches:
      "yes": s4
      "Approved with conditions → reassess": s2
      "High risk → change advisory": authority
      "Rejected": stop
  - id: s4
    do: "Record approval & notify"
    owner: "Change authority"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: release-6-1-2-1-s4-record-approval-and-notify

gate: "Change Approved"
criteria:
  - "Risk scored"
  - "Rollback linked"
  - "Window clear"
checks:
  - "Freeze and conflict check"
  - "Separation of duties"
on_failure:
  - "Move the window; check the calendar again"
  - "Reassign to an independent reviewer"
rework: "Conditions from the reviewer → reassess risk and update the record"

  - "docs/change-calendar.md"

  - "Approval lead time and rejections by reason — learning log"
```

files.body:
# Workflow 6.1.2.2 · Expedite an Emergency Change

When production is harmed and a fix cannot wait, raise an emergency change, approve it with the minimum checks, deploy it through the same pipeline, and review it within two working days.

**Run it:** ask your agent to "run `workflows/release-6-1-2-2-emergency-change.md` for {{initiative}}, stopping at every checkpoint", or use the command `release-6-1-2-2-run-emergency-change`. Each checkpoint means: show me the output and wait. At `decision` checkpoints the named person decides.

```yaml
workflow: release-6-1-2-2-emergency-change
title: "Expedite an Emergency Change"
owner: "Release manager"
inputs:
  - "docs/problem-record.md"
  - "docs/rollback-plan.md"
preconditions:
  - "Users are being harmed now"
  - "Rollback already tried or not possible"
steps:
  - id: s1
    do: "Raise the emergency change"
    owner: "Release manager"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: release-6-1-2-2-s1-raise-the-emergency-change
    skills: [itil-4]
    reviewers: [operations-reviewer]
    output: "docs/change-record.md"
    checkpoint: review-at-end
  - id: d1
    decision: "Truly an emergency?"
    owner: "Emergency change authority"
    agent: "prepare a decision brief — never decide"
    checkpoint: decision   # stop; Emergency change authority decides
    branches:
      "yes": s2
      "Not an emergency → normal change path": authority
  - id: s2
    do: "Approve with minimum checks"
    owner: "Emergency change authority"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: release-6-1-2-2-s2-approve-with-minimum-checks
    skills: [peer-review-of-changes]
    reviewers: [security-reviewer]
    output: "docs/change-approval.md"
    checkpoint: review-at-end
  - id: s3
    do: "Deploy through the same pipeline"
    owner: "DevOps / platform engineer"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: release-6-1-2-2-s3-deploy-through-the-same-pipeline
    reviewers: [devops-reviewer]
    output: "docs/deployment-record.md"
    checkpoint: review-at-end
    on:
      "Fix fails → raise again with what was learned": s1
  - id: s4
    do: "Review within two working days"
    owner: "Change authority"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: release-6-1-2-2-s4-review-within-two-working-days
    skills: [single-accountable-owner]
    reviewers: [governance-reviewer, compliance-reviewer]
    output: "docs/change-approval.md"
    checkpoint: review-at-end
    on:
      "Review finds misuse → recorded in the learning log": stop
gate: "Emergency Change Reviewed"
criteria:
  - "Users harmed now"
  - "Same pipeline, same build process"
checks:
  - "Post-implementation review within two working days"
on_failure:
  - "Post-review records the misuse; the change authority tightens the criteria"
  - "Rebuild through the pipeline and redeploy"
rework: "Fix failed → raise a new emergency change with what was learned"
outputs:
  - "docs/change-record.md"
  - "docs/change-approval.md"
  - "docs/deployment-record.md"
handoff: "Emergency change record & deployment record → 6.5.1 Run Smoke Checks; review → learning log"
learning:
  - "Emergency changes per month and how many were real — learning log"
```

# Workflow 6.2.4.1 · Roll Back or Roll Forward

Confirm the trigger, restore service by flag-off or redeploying the previous version, verify it, then decide to fix forward or withdraw and record why.

**Run it:** ask your agent to "run `workflows/release-6-2-4-1-recover.md` for {{initiative}}, stopping at every checkpoint", or use the command `release-6-2-4-1-run-recover`. Each checkpoint means: show me the output and wait. At `decision` checkpoints the named person decides.

```yaml
workflow: release-6-3-1-1-exposure-plan

  - id: s3

    decision: "Metrics emitting with baselines?"
```

# Workflow 6.3.2.1 · Run Ring 0

Turn the flag on for the pilot clerks, read every guardrail against its threshold through the soak, gather their feedback and decide on evidence.

**Run it:** ask your agent to "run `workflows/release-6-3-2-1-ring-0.md` for {{initiative}}, stopping at every checkpoint", or use the command `release-6-3-2-1-run-ring-0`. Each checkpoint means: show me the output and wait. At `decision` checkpoints the named person decides.

```yaml
title: "Run Ring 0"
owner: "Release manager"
inputs:
  - "docs/exposure-plan.md"
  - "docs/guardrail-metrics.md"
  - "docs/deployment-record.md"
preconditions:
  - "Smoke passed"
  - "Pilot users trained"
  - "Support briefed"
steps:
  - id: s1
    do: "Enable flag for Ring 0"
    owner: "Release manager"

    reviewers: [devops-reviewer]

    checkpoint: review-at-end
  - id: s2
    do: "Watch guardrails through the soak"
    owner: "Engineering lead"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: release-6-3-2-1-s2-watch-guardrails-through-the-soak
    skills: [soak-period, synthetic-monitoring]

  - id: s3
    do: "Collect pilot feedback"
    owner: "Product owner"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: release-6-3-2-1-s3-collect-pilot-feedback
    reviewers: [customer-reviewer, ux-reviewer, synthesiser]
    checkpoint: review-at-end
  - id: d1
    decision: "Healthy against thresholds?"
    owner: "Release manager"
    agent: "prepare a decision brief — never decide"
    checkpoint: decision   # stop; Release manager decides
    branches:
      "yes": s4
      "Too little data → extend soak": s2
      "Rollback threshold breached → recover": authority

  - id: s4
```

# Workflow 6.3.3.1 · Promote the Next Ring

For each next ring, check its entry criteria and blocking conditions, enable it, soak and read the guardrails, and record the promotion.

**Run it:** ask your agent to "run `workflows/release-6-3-3-1-promote.md` for {{initiative}}, stopping at every checkpoint", or use the command `release-6-3-3-1-run-promote`. Each checkpoint means: show me the output and wait. At `decision` checkpoints the named person decides.

```yaml
workflow: release-6-3-3-1-promote
title: "Promote the Next Ring"
owner: "Release manager"
inputs:
  - "docs/ring-record.md"
  - "docs/release-conditions.md"
  - "docs/launch-readiness.md"
  - "docs/exposure-plan.md"
preconditions:
  - "Previous ring healthy through its soak"
steps:
  - id: s1
    do: "Check next ring's entry criteria"
    owner: "Release manager"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: release-6-3-3-1-s1-check-next-ring-s-entry-criteria
    skills: [communication-matrix]
    reviewers: [support-reviewer, localization-reviewer, customer-reviewer]
    output: "docs/launch-readiness.md"
    checkpoint: review-at-end
  - id: s2
    do: "Check blocking conditions"
    owner: "Release manager"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: release-6-3-3-1-s2-check-blocking-conditions
    reviewers: [governance-reviewer]
    output: "docs/release-conditions.md"
    checkpoint: review-at-end
  - id: d1
    decision: "Ready to promote?"
    owner: "Release manager"
    agent: "prepare a decision brief — never decide"
    checkpoint: decision   # stop; Release manager decides
    branches:
      "yes": s3
      "Not ready → hold and recheck": s1
      "Condition overdue → owner & release manager": authority
      "Stop at the current ring": stop
  - id: s3
    do: "Enable the ring"
    owner: "Engineering lead"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: release-6-3-3-1-s3-enable-the-ring
    skills: [ring-deployment, feature-toggles]
    reviewers: [operations-reviewer]
    output: "docs/flag-log.md"
    checkpoint: review-at-end
  - id: s4
    do: "Soak & read guardrails"
    owner: "Engineering lead"

    on:
      "Breach → 6.3.4 guardrail response": authority
  - id: s5
    do: "Record the promotion"
    owner: "Release manager"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: release-6-3-3-1-s5-record-the-promotion
    reviewers: [devops-reviewer]

    checkpoint: review-at-end
    on:
      "Next ring": s1
gate: "Ring Promotion"
criteria:
  - "Entry criteria met"
  - "Blocking conditions closed with evidence"
checks:
  - "Guardrails through the soak"
on_failure:
  - "Pull the ring's flag; close the condition first"
  - "Return to one ring at a time"
rework: "Not ready → hold the ring and recheck its entry criteria"
outputs:
  - "docs/ring-record.md"
  - "docs/flag-log.md"
handoff: "Ring promotion records → 6.5.2 Verify Production Against Predictions; launch announcements timed by 6.4.2"
learning:
  - "Rings held and why — learning log"
```

files.body:
# Workflow 6.3.4.1 · Respond to a Guardrail Reading

When a guardrail crosses a threshold, confirm the reading, pause the ring or roll back as agreed, diagnose and fix safely, then resume — and record each step.

**Run it:** ask your agent to "run `workflows/release-6-3-4-1-guardrails.md` for {{initiative}}, stopping at every checkpoint", or use the command `release-6-3-4-1-run-guardrails`. Each checkpoint means: show me the output and wait. At `decision` checkpoints the named person decides.

```yaml
workflow: release-6-3-4-1-guardrails
title: "Respond to a Guardrail Reading"
owner: "On-call engineer"
inputs:
  - "docs/guardrail-metrics.md"
  - "docs/exposure-plan.md"
  - "docs/runbook.md"
preconditions:
  - "A ring is exposed"
  - "Alerts wired"
steps:
  - id: s1
    do: "Confirm the reading"
    owner: "On-call engineer"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: release-6-3-4-1-s1-confirm-the-reading
```
