```yaml
    reviewers: [reliability-reviewer, data-reviewer]
    output: "docs/guardrail-metrics.md"
    checkpoint: review-at-end
  - id: d1
    decision: "Pause or rollback threshold?"
    owner: "On-call engineer"
    agent: "prepare a decision brief — never decide"
    checkpoint: decision   # stop; On-call engineer decides
    branches:
      "yes": s2
      "Rollback threshold or harm → 6.2.4 / incident command": authority
  - id: s2
    do: "Pause the ring"
    owner: "On-call engineer"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: release-6-3-4-1-s2-pause-the-ring
    skills: [kill-switch, feature-toggles]
    reviewers: [customer-reviewer, support-reviewer]
    output: "docs/flag-log.md"
    checkpoint: review-at-end
  - id: s3
    do: "Diagnose & fix safely"
    owner: "Engineering lead"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: release-6-3-4-1-s3-diagnose-and-fix-safely
    skills: [soak-period]
    reviewers: [ai-reviewer, devops-reviewer]
    output: "docs/problem-record.md"
    checkpoint: review-at-end
    on:
      "Fix didn't hold → stay paused": s2
      "Unfixable → kill switch, withdraw": stop
  - id: s4
    do: "Resume & record"
    owner: "Release manager"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: release-6-3-4-1-s4-resume-and-record
    skills: [guardrail-metrics]
    reviewers: [operations-reviewer]
    output: "docs/ring-record.md"
    checkpoint: review-at-end

criteria:
  - "Action within minutes of a confirmed breach"
checks:
  - "Second source for the reading"
on_failure:
  - "Release manager pauses and records the delay"
  - "Restore the original threshold; record the breach"
rework: "Fix didn't hold → stay paused and diagnose again"
outputs:
  - "docs/guardrail-metrics.md"
  - "docs/ring-record.md"
  - "docs/flag-log.md"
handoff: "Ring decision → 6.3.3 Promote Through the Rings; problem record → OPERATE problem backlog"
learning:
  - "Breaches and time to act — learning log"
```

files.body:
# Workflow 6.5.1.1 · Run the Smoke Checks

Right after deployment, run health checks and smoke the critical path and the fallback with test data, then start continuous synthetic checks.

**Run it:** ask your agent to "run `workflows/release-6-5-1-1-smoke.md` for {{initiative}}, stopping at every checkpoint", or use the command `release-6-5-1-1-run-smoke`. Each checkpoint means: show me the output and wait. At `decision` checkpoints the named person decides.

```yaml
workflow: release-6-5-1-1-smoke
title: "Run the Smoke Checks"
owner: "CI/CD pipeline"
inputs:
  - "docs/deployment-record.md"
  - "docs/test-evidence.md"
preconditions:
  - "Deployment finished"
  - "Test tenant available"
steps:
  - id: s1
    do: "Run health checks"
    owner: "CI/CD pipeline"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: release-6-5-1-1-s1-run-health-checks
    skills: [health-checks]
    reviewers: [infrastructure-reviewer]
    checkpoint: review-at-end
  - id: s2
    do: "Smoke critical path & fallback"
    owner: "CI/CD pipeline"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: release-6-5-1-1-s2-smoke-critical-path-and-fallback
    skills: [smoke-testing, dark-launch]
    reviewers: [quality-reviewer, privacy-reviewer]
    output: "docs/smoke-results.md"
    checkpoint: review-at-end
  - id: d1
    decision: "All passed?"
    owner: "Release manager"
    agent: "prepare a decision brief — never decide"
    checkpoint: decision   # stop; Release manager decides
    branches:
      "yes": s3
      "Flaky → re-run once": s2
      "Fails → rollback decision": authority
      "Rolled back → release paused": stop
  - id: s3
    do: "Start synthetic checks"
    owner: "DevOps / platform engineer"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: release-6-5-1-1-s3-start-synthetic-checks
    skills: [synthetic-monitoring, site-reliability-engineering]
    reviewers: [devops-reviewer]
    output: "docs/smoke-results.md"
    checkpoint: review-at-end
  - id: s4
    do: "Record results"
    owner: "DevOps / platform engineer"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: release-6-5-1-1-s4-record-results
    skills: [guardrail-metrics]
    reviewers: [data-reviewer]
    output: "docs/smoke-results.md"
    checkpoint: review-at-end
gate: "Smoke Passed"
criteria:
  - "Critical path and fallback pass"
checks:
  - "Pipeline-run checks"
on_failure:
  - "Roll back per the plan"
  - "Cancel the order and fix the check to use the test tenant"
rework: "Flaky check → re-run once, then fix the check"
outputs:
  - "docs/smoke-results.md"
  - "docs/smoke-results.md"
handoff: "Smoke check results → 6.3.2 Run Ring 0 and 6.5.2 Verify Production Against Predictions"
learning:
  - "Failures smoke caught, and ones it missed — learning log"
```

# Workflow 6.5.2.1 · Verify Production Against Predictions

List every prediction the release made, read each in production, compare claim with evidence, route what doesn't match, and report after the soak.

**Run it:** ask your agent to "run `workflows/release-6-5-2-1-verify-prod.md` for {{initiative}}, stopping at every checkpoint", or use the command `release-6-5-2-1-run-verify-prod`. Each checkpoint means: show me the output and wait. At `decision` checkpoints the named person decides.

```yaml
workflow: release-6-5-2-1-verify-prod
title: "Verify Production Against Predictions"
owner: "Release manager"
inputs:
  - "docs/guardrail-metrics.md"
  - "docs/ring-record.md"
  - "docs/smoke-results.md"
  - "docs/nft-summary.md"
preconditions:
  - "Full exposure or a stable ring"
  - "Metrics emitting"
steps:
  - id: s1
    do: "List every prediction"
    owner: "Release manager"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: release-6-5-2-1-s1-list-every-prediction
    skills: [decision-record]
    reviewers: [architecture-reviewer, product-reviewer]
    checkpoint: review-at-end
  - id: s2
    do: "Read each in production"
    owner: "SRE"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: release-6-5-2-1-s2-read-each-in-production
    skills: [synthetic-monitoring]
    reviewers: [performance-reviewer, data-reviewer, synthesiser]
    output: "docs/guardrail-metrics.md"
    checkpoint: review-at-end
  - id: s3
    do: "Compare claim with evidence"
    owner: "Release manager"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: release-6-5-2-1-s3-compare-claim-with-evidence
    skills: [production-verification]
    reviewers: [reliability-reviewer, business-reviewer, synthesiser]
    output: "docs/pdv-report.md"
    checkpoint: review-at-end
  - id: d1
    decision: "Matches what we said?"
    owner: "Release manager"
    agent: "prepare a decision brief — never decide"
    checkpoint: decision   # stop; Release manager decides
    branches:
      "yes": s4
      "Measurement gap → fix & re-read": s2
      "All match → report": s5
      "Badly missed → release manager & architect": authority
  - id: s4
    do: "Route mismatches"
    owner: "Engineering lead"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: release-6-5-2-1-s4-route-mismatches
    reviewers: [operations-reviewer]
    output: "docs/problem-record.md"
    checkpoint: review-at-end
  - id: s5

    skills: [soak-period]
    reviewers: [reliability-reviewer]
    output: "docs/pdv-report.md"
    checkpoint: review-at-end
    on:
      "Production check failed → roll back, close as failed": stop
gate: "Production Verified"
criteria:
  - "Every prediction read"
  - "Soak complete"
checks:
  - "SRE second review"
on_failure:
  - "Rewrite as claim vs evidence"
  - "Record the gap; capture the baseline for the next release"
rework: "Measurement gap → fix the instrumentation and read again"
outputs:
  - "docs/pdv-report.md"
  - "docs/pdv-report.md"
handoff: "Post-deployment verification report → 6.5.4 Close the Release & Hand Over"
learning:
  - "Predictions that were wrong, and by how much — learning log"
```

# Workflow 6.5.3.1 · Run Hypercare

**Run it:** ask your agent to "run `workflows/release-6-5-3-1-hypercare.md` for {{initiative}}, stopping at every checkpoint", or use the command `release-6-5-3-1-run-hypercare`. Each checkpoint means: show me the output and wait. At `decision` checkpoints the named person decides.

# Process 6.5 · Post-Deployment Verification

Prove in production that the release does what it said, catch early-life problems, and hand a runnable service to OPERATE.

**Run it:** ask your agent to "run `workflows/release-6-5-verify-prod.md` for {{initiative}}, stopping at every checkpoint", or use the command `release-6-5-run-verify-prod`. Each checkpoint means: show me the output and wait. At `decision` checkpoints the named person decides.

```yaml
orchestration: release-6-5-verify-prod
title: "Post-Deployment Verification"
owner: "SRE, Support lead, Engineering lead"
inputs:
  - "docs/deployment-record.md"
  - "docs/ring-record.md"
  - "docs/guardrail-metrics.md"
  - "docs/runbook.md"
entry:
  - "Deployment finished"
  - "Rings exposed and metrics emitting"
runs:
  - unit: "6.5.1 Run Smoke Checks"
    spec: workflows/release-6-5-1-smoke.md
    command: release-6-5-1-run-smoke
    gate: "Smoke Passed"
    checkpoint: review   # show outputs, wait for go-ahead
  - unit: "6.5.2 Verify Production Against Predictions"
    spec: workflows/release-6-5-2-verify.md
    command: release-6-5-2-run-verify
    gate: "Production Verified"
    checkpoint: review   # show outputs, wait for go-ahead
  - unit: "6.5.3 Run Hypercare"
    spec: workflows/release-6-5-3-hypercare.md
    command: release-6-5-3-run-hypercare
    gate: "Hypercare Exit"
    checkpoint: review   # show outputs, wait for go-ahead
  - unit: "6.5.4 Close the Release & Hand Over to OPERATE"
    spec: workflows/release-6-5-4-close.md
    command: release-6-5-4-run-close
    gate: "Release Closed"
    checkpoint: review   # show outputs, wait for go-ahead
parallel:
  - "Hypercare overlaps the later rings and the soak"
gate: "Release Closed"
decided_by: "Release manager judges the production check and closes the release; the operations lead accepts the service."
criteria:
  - "Every prediction has a reading"
  - "Soak complete"
  - "Operations acceptance in writing"
routes:
  forward: "Closed release, runbook, SLOs → OPERATE; retrospective and learning log → EVOLVE"
  rework: "Measurement gap → re-read; rejected handover → fill the gaps"
  alternate: "Early outcome readings → EVOLVE outcome review"
  escalate: "Smoke fails or prediction badly missed → release manager; Sev-1/2 → incident command"
  stop: "Production check failed → roll back; release closed as failed — recorded in the learning log"
outputs:
  - "docs/smoke-results.md"
  - "docs/pdv-report.md"
  - "docs/hypercare-log.md"
  - "docs/operate-handover.md"
  - "docs/release-record.md"
  - "docs/release-retro.md"
  - "docs/learning-log.md"
handoff: "Closed release record, operational handover, runbook and SLOs → OPERATE; release retrospective → EVOLVE"
```

# Act RELEASE · Release

Move verified change into production safely and reversibly, on a recorded decision, with the people who use and support it ready.

**Run it:** ask your agent to "run `workflows/release-act.md` for {{initiative}}, stopping at every checkpoint", or use the command `release-run-act`. Each checkpoint means: show me the output and wait. At `decision` checkpoints the named person decides.

```yaml
orchestration: release-act
title: "RELEASE"
owner: "Engineering lead, DevOps / platform engineer, Support lead"
inputs:
  - "docs/quality-gate-record.md"
  - "docs/verified-increment.md"
  - "docs/build-artifact.md"
  - "docs/runbook.md"
entry:
  - "Quality gate record (VERIFY) passed or conditionally passed"
  - "Verified increments against a named build"
  - "Runbook and release build from BUILD"
runs:
  - unit: "6.1 Release Prep & Change Approval"
    spec: workflows/release-6-1-prep-and-approve.md
    command: release-6-1-run-prep-and-approve
    gate: "Go / No-Go"
    checkpoint: review   # show outputs, wait for go-ahead
  - unit: "6.2 Deployment"
    spec: workflows/release-6-2-deploy.md
    command: release-6-2-run-deploy
    gate: "Deployed with Rollback Proven"
    checkpoint: review   # show outputs, wait for go-ahead
  - unit: "6.3 Progressive Rollout"
    spec: workflows/release-6-3-rollout.md
    command: release-6-3-run-rollout
    gate: "Full Exposure"
    checkpoint: review   # show outputs, wait for go-ahead
  - unit: "6.4 Launch Readiness"
    spec: workflows/release-6-4-launch-ready.md
    command: release-6-4-run-launch-ready
    gate: "Launch Readiness"
    checkpoint: review   # show outputs, wait for go-ahead
  - unit: "6.5 Post-Deployment Verification"
    spec: workflows/release-6-5-verify-prod.md
    command: release-6-5-run-verify-prod
    gate: "Release Closed"
    checkpoint: review   # show outputs, wait for go-ahead
parallel:
  - "6.4 runs alongside 6.1 — launch readiness is a Go / No-Go input"
  - "Deployment planning and rehearsal (6.2.1–6.2.2) and the exposure plan (6.3.1) run before the go"
  - "Hypercare (6.5.3) overlaps the later rings"
gate: "Go / No-Go"
decided_by: "Release manager decides go / no-go and ring promotion; sponsor is the release authority for disputes; on-call may pull the kill switch without asking."
criteria:
  - "Every in-scope story verified against the release build"
  - "No open Sev-1/2 defects"
  - "Non-functional criteria demonstrated"
  - "Rollback exercised in staging"
  - "Success metrics emitting before enablement"
  - "Out-of-scope list agreed"
  - "Change approved"
  - "Launch readiness confirmed"
routes:
  forward: "Healthy and verified → OPERATE (Act VII) with the release record, runbook and SLOs"
  rework: "Guardrail breach → roll back (6.2.4); no-go → back to VERIFY, BUILD or 6.1.1 as the failing criterion says"
  alternate: "Pause at the current ring; conditions hold the rings they block"
  escalate: "Go / No-Go dispute → sponsor as release authority; severity breach → incident command"

outputs:
  - "docs/release-candidate.md"
  - "docs/change-record.md"
  - "docs/go-no-go-record.md"

  - "docs/release-record.md"
  - "docs/learning-log.md"
```

# AGENTS.md — {{initiative}}

> Node SDLC · Act VI RELEASE · Scale: Product team. Read this first, every session.

## How we work
People own the work, agents help do it. In every unit the person in the role briefs the agent, gives it the right context, checks what it produces, and makes every decision. The agent drafts, researches, analyses, structures and checks — it never decides, approves or signs.
- **You:** Choose what to work on · give context · make decisions · review and correct · sign off · own the artifact
- **Your agent:** Draft · research · summarise · structure into templates · spot gaps and risks · check against criteria · prepare options

## Where this act sits
RELEASE is part of the **Delivery track** — Are we building the thing right? The acts keep their order as a logical dependency — a problem is validated before it is planned, designed before it is built — but they are kinds of work that run continuously and in parallel, at different sizes, not phases on a calendar.

## RELEASE: Move verified change into production safely, reversibly and on a recorded decision, with the organisation ready to support it.
- **6.1 Release Prep & Change Approval** — gate: Go / No-Go. Produces: Release candidate, Change record, Release notes, Go / No-Go decision record, Conditions register.
- **6.2 Deployment** — gate: Deployed with Rollback Proven. Produces: Deployment plan, Rollback plan, Staging rehearsal record, Deployment record, Rollback record.
- **6.3 Progressive Rollout** — gate: Full Exposure. Produces: Exposure plan, Guardrail definitions, Ring record, Flag change log.
- **6.4 Launch Readiness** — gate: Launch Readiness. Produces: Support enablement pack, Communications plan, User documentation, Training record, Launch readiness record.
- **6.5 Post-Deployment Verification** — gate: Release Closed. Produces: Smoke check results, Post-deployment verification report, Hypercare log, Operational handover pack, Release record, Release retrospective, Learning log.
- Act gate: **Go / No-Go** — decided by: Release manager decides go / no-go and ring promotion; sponsor is the release authority for disputes; on-call may pull the kill switch without asking..

## Conventions
- Artifacts live in `docs/<artifact>.md`, written from `templates/<artifact>.md`.
- Every artifact carries its trace ID and links the IDs upstream of it; register new IDs in `TRACE.md`.
- Trace chain: RC → CHG → GNG → DEP → RING → LCH → RN → PDV → LRN.
- Log each step in `PROGRESS.md`.
- Before saving, score the artifact against `rubrics/<artifact>.md`.

## Your toolkit
- `commands/` — one per step, workflow, subprocess, process and the act. Start with `release-run-act` or the unit you're on.
- `workflows/` — run specs with checkpoints; stop at every checkpoint.
- `skills/` — how-to packages for each technique; load the ones a command names.
- `agents/` — reviewers by lens, plus researcher, synthesiser, challenger and decision-brief writer.
- `TOOLS.md` and `GUARDRAILS.md` — what you may use and must never do.

## Ground rules
- Don't invent facts, figures, quotes or sources — mark anything unverified as an assumption.
- If something you need is missing, ask me instead of guessing.
- Keep personal or confidential data out unless I've provided it for this purpose.
- Prepare decisions; don't make them — I decide.

## Scale: Product team
Write for a product trio and a delivery team. Use our shared templates, make outputs ready to drop into the backlog or repository, and flag anything that needs the team's refinement.
Access: Read and write the shared workspace and backlog; agents propose changes, people merge and publish.
team.GUARDRAILS.md:
# Guardrails & hooks — Release

People own the work, agents help do it. In every unit the person in the role briefs the agent, gives it the right context, checks what it produces, and makes every decision. The agent drafts, researches, analyses, structures and checks — it never decides, approves or signs.

## Always
- Don't invent facts, figures, quotes or sources — mark anything unverified as an assumption.
- If something you need is missing, ask me instead of guessing.
- Keep personal or confidential data out unless I've provided it for this purpose.
- Prepare decisions; don't make them — I decide.
- Never paste passwords, keys, or personal data you aren't allowed to share — anonymise first
- At enterprise scale, use only approved tools
- Check every fact, number and source the agent gives you
- Agents prepare decisions; people make them
- Save the output in the artifact template and note that an agent helped
- If the agent's output is wrong, correct the prompt or the context — then record what you learned

## Scale: Product team
- Read and write the shared workspace and backlog; agents propose changes, people merge and publish.
- Watch for: Each person's agent producing inconsistent artifacts — use the shared templates
- Watch for: Discovery and delivery drifting apart

## Hooks — automatic where your agent supports them, a checklist everywhere else
| When | Check | If it fails |
|---|---|---|
| Before saving an artifact | It follows its template · it carries its trace ID and links upstream IDs · every claim cites evidence or is marked 'Assumption:' · no personal data or secrets | Fix, or stop and tell me |
| Before a decision step | Stop. Prepare the decision brief. Wait for the named decision-maker | Never decide or approve |
| Before anything leaves the team | Messages, posts, invitations and shared documents are drafts until a person sends them | Ask for approval |
| Before using a new tool or data source | Is it allowed at this scale? Is the data allowed in this tool? | Ask first |
| After each step | Append to PROGRESS.md: date, unit, what was done, artifacts, decisions, open questions, next | Always |

## Rules and policies by unit
### RELEASE
- A go — named person, date, outcome — is the only thing that makes stories Released
- Scope (only verified stories) is never conditional
- Every condition has an owner, evidence and a due date
- Every rollback raises a problem record; every release, including a rolled-back one, ends with a retrospective
- Change management per ISO/IEC 20000-1
- No exposure before support, comms, docs and training are ready
- Change windows and freezes
- Decision rights

### 6.1 Release Prep & Change Approval
- Scope is never conditional
- A go is the only thing that makes stories Released
- Change policy per ISO/IEC 20000-1
- Decider named before the release
- Change windows and freezes

### 6.1.1 Assemble the Release Candidate
- A story cannot be in two open releases
- Scope — only verified stories — is never conditional
- Requesters of excluded work are told before deployment
- Only verified stories
- The release window

### 6.1.2 Raise & Approve the Change
- No production change without an approved change record
- Emergency changes reviewed within two working days
- Change policy per ISO/IEC 20000-1
- Security review for new data flows
- Change freezes
- Business peak hours

### 6.1.3 Write Release Notes
- Never describe what is not in the build
- Plain language, written for each audience
- Release scope

### 6.1.4 Hold the Go / No-Go Decision
- Scope — only verified stories — is never conditional
- A go is the only thing that makes stories Released
- A no-go names what must change
- The decider is named before the release, not during it
- Release window
- Decision rights

### 6.2 Deployment
- No deployment without a recorded go and an approved change
- No manual changes in production
- Build once, deploy many
- Deploy outside business peaks
- Change window
- Data migrations

### 6.2.1 Plan the Deployment & Rollback
- No manual changes in production
- No contract migration in the same release as its expand
- Build once, deploy many
- Window length
- Data migrations

### 6.2.2 Rehearse & Prove Rollback
- An unrehearsed rollback fails the Go / No-Go
- Rehearse every release, not only the 'big' ones
- Staging parity

### 6.2.3 Deploy to Production
- No deployment without a recorded go and an approved change
- No hand edits in production
- Deploy outside business peaks
- Change window

### 6.2.4 Roll Back or Roll Forward
- Roll back first, diagnose later
- A roll-forward is a new change with its own go
- Every rollback raises a problem record
- Time to restore

### 6.3 Progressive Rollout
- Thresholds set before exposure and never moved after
- One ring at a time
- Every release flag has an owner and a removal date
- Site freezes
- Open conditions

### 6.3.1 Configure Flags & Exposure Plan
- Thresholds are set before exposure and never moved after
- Every release flag has an owner and a removal date
- Site freezes
- Flag capability in the build

### 6.3.2 Run Ring 0 (Canary)
- Never promote on a breached threshold
- Ring 0 users are trained and know how to report
- Soak time
- Pilot volume

### 6.3.3 Promote Through the Rings
- One ring at a time
- No promotion inside a freeze
- Users told and trained before their ring
- Freezes
- Open conditions

### 6.3.4 Watch Guardrails, Pause or Roll Back
- Rollback threshold breached → roll back, no debate
- Every pause and resume logged
- Pre-agreed thresholds

### 6.4 Launch Readiness
- No ring enabled for untrained or unsupported users
- Localised for every site in scope
- WCAG 2.2 AA for user documentation
- Translation lead time
- Shift patterns

### 6.4.1 Enable Support
- No exposure before support is briefed
- Hypercare length and exit criteria set in advance
- Support capacity

### 6.4.2 Plan & Send Launch Communications
- Never announce a date a ring hasn't confirmed
- Localised for each site
- Ring dates

### 6.4.3 Publish User & Operational Documentation
- Docs versioned with the release
- Localised for every site in scope
- Translation lead time

### 6.4.4 Train Users & Confirm Readiness
- No ring enabled for untrained users
- Readiness is confirmed per ring, not once
- Shift patterns
- Languages

### 6.5 Post-Deployment Verification
- No release closed without a production check
- Mismatches become defects, problems or ADR updates
- Every release gets a retrospective
- Flags removed on a scheduled date
- Soak length
- Operations acceptance criteria

### 6.5.1 Run Smoke Checks
- No exposure before smoke passes
- Smoke never uses real customer data
- Synthetic checks stay on after the release
- No real data in smoke

### 6.5.2 Verify Production Against Predictions
- A release is not closed without a production check
- Claims cite numbers, not adjectives
- Mismatches become defects, problems or ADR updates — never notes
- Soak length
- Measurement maturity

### 6.5.3 Run Hypercare
- Every defect routed to the backlog with severity and owner
- The building team stays on hand during hypercare
- Team availability

### 6.5.4 Close the Release & Hand Over to OPERATE
- Closed only after the production check and soak
- Change record closed with its outcome
- Every release gets a retrospective
- Operations acceptance criteria

# Workflow 6.1.1.1 · Assemble the Release Candidate

Assemble the release story by story from verified increments, with an objective, explicit exclusions and owners for every dependency and gate condition.

**Run it:** ask your agent to "run `workflows/release-6-1-1-1-assemble-rc.md` for {{initiative}}, stopping at every checkpoint", or use the command `release-6-1-1-1-run-assemble-rc`. Each checkpoint means: show me the output and wait. At `decision` checkpoints the named person decides.

```yaml

title: "Assemble the Release Candidate"
owner: "Release manager"
inputs:
  - "docs/quality-gate-record.md"
  - "docs/verified-increment.md"
  - "docs/build-artifact.md"
preconditions:
  - "Quality gate passed or conditionally passed"
  - "Release build in the registry"
steps:
  - id: s1
    do: "Write the release objective"
    owner: "Release manager"

    output: "docs/release-candidate.md"

  - id: s2
    do: "Pick verified stories"
    owner: "Release manager"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"

    skills: [build-once-deploy-many]
    reviewers: [devops-reviewer, customer-reviewer]
    output: "docs/release-candidate.md"
    checkpoint: review
    on:
      "Nothing worth releasing": stop
  - id: d1
    decision: "Verified against the release build?"
    owner: "QA lead"
    agent: "prepare a decision brief — never decide"
    checkpoint: decision   # stop; QA lead decides
    branches:
      "yes": s3
      "Wrong build → re-verify or drop": s2
  - id: s3

  - "docs/release-candidate.md"
```

```yaml
inputs:

  - "Rollback plan drafted"

  - id: s2

  - id: s3
```

# Workflow 6.5.4.2 · Hold the Release Retrospective

Whatever the outcome, walk the release from assembly to close, read the DORA measures, decide what to keep and change, give every change an owner and log it.

**Run it:** ask your agent to "run `workflows/release-6-5-4-2-release-retro.md` for {{initiative}}, stopping at every checkpoint", or use the command `release-6-5-4-2-run-release-retro`. Each checkpoint means: show me the output and wait. At `decision` checkpoints the named person decides.

```yaml

title: "Hold the Release Retrospective"
owner: "Release manager"
inputs:
  - "docs/release-record.md"
  - "docs/pdv-report.md"
  - "docs/hypercare-log.md"
preconditions:
  - "Release closed (passed, passed with issues, failed or rolled back)"
steps:
  - id: s1
    do: "Build the release timeline"
    owner: "Release manager"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: release-6-5-4-2-s1-build-the-release-timeline
    reviewers: [governance-reviewer]
    output: "docs/release-record.md"

  - id: s2

    owner: "Release manager"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: release-6-5-4-2-s2-read-the-dora-measures
    skills: [dora-metrics]
    reviewers: [operations-reviewer]
    checkpoint: review
  - id: s3
    do: "Run the blameless retrospective"
    owner: "Release manager"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: release-6-5-4-2-s3-run-the-blameless-retrospective
    skills: [retrospective]
    reviewers: [support-reviewer, reliability-reviewer]
    output: "docs/release-retro.md"
    checkpoint: review
  - id: d1

    owner: "Release manager"
    agent: "prepare a decision brief — never decide"
    checkpoint: decision   # stop; Release manager decides
    branches:
      "yes": s4
      "Changes without owners → assign": s3
  - id: s4
    do: "Log learning & feed EVOLVE"
    owner: "Release manager"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: release-6-5-4-2-s4-log-learning-and-feed-evolve
    reviewers: [product-reviewer]

  - "docs/learning-log.md"
```

# AGENTS.md — {{initiative}}

> Node SDLC · Act VI RELEASE · Scale: Enterprise. Read this first, every session.

## How we work
People own the work, agents help do it. In every unit the person in the role briefs the agent, gives it the right context, checks what it produces, and makes every decision. The agent drafts, researches, analyses, structures and checks — it never decides, approves or signs.
- **You:** Choose what to work on · give context · make decisions · review and correct · sign off · own the artifact
- **Your agent:** Draft · research · summarise · structure into templates · spot gaps and risks · check against criteria · prepare options

## Where this act sits
RELEASE is part of the **Delivery track** — Are we building the thing right? The acts keep their order as a logical dependency — a problem is validated before it is planned, designed before it is built — but they are kinds of work that run continuously and in parallel, at different sizes, not phases on a calendar.

## RELEASE: Move verified change into production safely, reversibly and on a recorded decision, with the organisation ready to support it.
- **6.1 Release Prep & Change Approval** — gate: Go / No-Go. Produces: Release candidate, Change record, Release notes, Go / No-Go decision record, Conditions register.
- **6.2 Deployment** — gate: Deployed with Rollback Proven. Produces: Deployment plan, Rollback plan, Staging rehearsal record, Deployment record, Rollback record.
- **6.3 Progressive Rollout** — gate: Full Exposure. Produces: Exposure plan, Guardrail definitions, Ring record, Flag change log.
- **6.4 Launch Readiness** — gate: Launch Readiness. Produces: Support enablement pack, Communications plan, User documentation, Training record, Launch readiness record.
- **6.5 Post-Deployment Verification** — gate: Release Closed. Produces: Smoke check results, Post-deployment verification report, Hypercare log, Operational handover pack, Release record, Release retrospective, Learning log.
- Act gate: **Go / No-Go** — decided by: Release manager decides go / no-go and ring promotion; sponsor is the release authority for disputes; on-call may pull the kill switch without asking..

## Conventions
- Artifacts live in `docs/<artifact>.md`, written from `templates/<artifact>.md`.
- Every artifact carries its trace ID and links the IDs upstream of it; register new IDs in `TRACE.md`.
- Trace chain: RC → CHG → GNG → DEP → RING → LCH → RN → PDV → LRN.
- Log each step in `PROGRESS.md`.
- Before saving, score the artifact against `rubrics/<artifact>.md`.

## Your toolkit
- `commands/` — one per step, workflow, subprocess, process and the act. Start with `release-run-act` or the unit you're on.
- `workflows/` — run specs with checkpoints; stop at every checkpoint.
- `skills/` — how-to packages for each technique; load the ones a command names.
- `agents/` — reviewers by lens, plus researcher, synthesiser, challenger and decision-brief writer.
- `TOOLS.md` and `GUARDRAILS.md` — what you may use and must never do.

## Ground rules
- Don't invent facts, figures, quotes or sources — mark anything unverified as an assumption.
- If something you need is missing, ask me instead of guessing.
- Keep personal or confidential data out unless I've provided it for this purpose.
- Prepare decisions; don't make them — I decide.

## Scale: Enterprise
Use formal language and our approved templates. Back every claim with a reference to its evidence for audit, flag compliance, security and privacy implications, name the approver for each decision, and keep confidential details out of anything meant for wider sharing.
Access: Approved tools only; read-only on customer and production data; every write goes through review; agent actions logged for audit.

# Guardrails & hooks — Release

People own the work, agents help do it. In every unit the person in the role briefs the agent, gives it the right context, checks what it produces, and makes every decision. The agent drafts, researches, analyses, structures and checks — it never decides, approves or signs.

## Always
- Don't invent facts, figures, quotes or sources — mark anything unverified as an assumption.
- If something you need is missing, ask me instead of guessing.
- Keep personal or confidential data out unless I've provided it for this purpose.
- Prepare decisions; don't make them — I decide.
- Never paste passwords, keys, or personal data you aren't allowed to share — anonymise first
- At enterprise scale, use only approved tools
- Check every fact, number and source the agent gives you
- Agents prepare decisions; people make them
- Save the output in the artifact template and note that an agent helped
- If the agent's output is wrong, correct the prompt or the context — then record what you learned

## Scale: Enterprise
- Approved tools only; read-only on customer and production data; every write goes through review; agent actions logged for audit.
- Watch for: Pasting confidential or personal data into unapproved tools
- Watch for: Agent output in audited artifacts without a human reviewer named

## Hooks — automatic where your agent supports them, a checklist everywhere else
| When | Check | If it fails |
|---|---|---|
| Before saving an artifact | It follows its template · it carries its trace ID and links upstream IDs · every claim cites evidence or is marked 'Assumption:' · no personal data or secrets | Fix, or stop and tell me |
| Before a decision step | Stop. Prepare the decision brief. Wait for the named decision-maker | Never decide or approve |
| Before anything leaves the team | Messages, posts, invitations and shared documents are drafts until a person sends them | Ask for approval |
| Before using a new tool or data source | Is it allowed at this scale? Is the data allowed in this tool? | Ask first |
| After each step | Append to PROGRESS.md: date, unit, what was done, artifacts, decisions, open questions, next | Always |

## Rules and policies by unit
### RELEASE
- A go — named person, date, outcome — is the only thing that makes stories Released
- Scope (only verified stories) is never conditional
- Every condition has an owner, evidence and a due date
- Every rollback raises a problem record; every release, including a rolled-back one, ends with a retrospective
- Change management per ISO/IEC 20000-1
- No exposure before support, comms, docs and training are ready
- Change windows and freezes
- Decision rights

### 6.1 Release Prep & Change Approval
- Scope is never conditional
- A go is the only thing that makes stories Released
- Change policy per ISO/IEC 20000-1
- Decider named before the release
- Change windows and freezes

### 6.1.1 Assemble the Release Candidate
- A story cannot be in two open releases
- Scope — only verified stories — is never conditional
- Requesters of excluded work are told before deployment
- Only verified stories
- The release window

### 6.1.2 Raise & Approve the Change
- No production change without an approved change record
- Emergency changes reviewed within two working days
- Change policy per ISO/IEC 20000-1
- Security review for new data flows
- Change freezes
- Business peak hours

### 6.1.3 Write Release Notes
- Never describe what is not in the build
- Plain language, written for each audience
- Release scope

### 6.1.4 Hold the Go / No-Go Decision
- Scope — only verified stories — is never conditional
- A go is the only thing that makes stories Released
- A no-go names what must change
- The decider is named before the release, not during it
- Release window
- Decision rights

### 6.2 Deployment
- No deployment without a recorded go and an approved change
- No manual changes in production
- Build once, deploy many
- Deploy outside business peaks
- Change window
- Data migrations

### 6.2.1 Plan the Deployment & Rollback
- No manual changes in production
- No contract migration in the same release as its expand
- Build once, deploy many
- Window length
- Data migrations

### 6.2.2 Rehearse & Prove Rollback
- An unrehearsed rollback fails the Go / No-Go
- Rehearse every release, not only the 'big' ones
- Staging parity

### 6.2.3 Deploy to Production
- No deployment without a recorded go and an approved change
- No hand edits in production
- Deploy outside business peaks
- Change window

### 6.2.4 Roll Back or Roll Forward
- Roll back first, diagnose later
- A roll-forward is a new change with its own go
- Every rollback raises a problem record
- Time to restore

### 6.3 Progressive Rollout
- Thresholds set before exposure and never moved after
- One ring at a time
- Every release flag has an owner and a removal date
- Site freezes
- Open conditions

### 6.3.1 Configure Flags & Exposure Plan
- Thresholds are set before exposure and never moved after
- Every release flag has an owner and a removal date
- Site freezes
- Flag capability in the build

### 6.3.2 Run Ring 0 (Canary)
- Never promote on a breached threshold
- Ring 0 users are trained and know how to report
- Soak time
- Pilot volume

### 6.3.3 Promote Through the Rings
- One ring at a time
- No promotion inside a freeze
- Users told and trained before their ring
- Freezes
- Open conditions

### 6.3.4 Watch Guardrails, Pause or Roll Back
- Rollback threshold breached → roll back, no debate
- Every pause and resume logged
- Pre-agreed thresholds

### 6.4 Launch Readiness
- No ring enabled for untrained or unsupported users
- Localised for every site in scope
- WCAG 2.2 AA for user documentation
- Translation lead time
- Shift patterns

### 6.4.1 Enable Support
- No exposure before support is briefed
- Hypercare length and exit criteria set in advance
- Support capacity

### 6.4.2 Plan & Send Launch Communications
- Never announce a date a ring hasn't confirmed
- Localised for each site
- Ring dates

### 6.4.3 Publish User & Operational Documentation
- Docs versioned with the release
- Localised for every site in scope
- Translation lead time

### 6.4.4 Train Users & Confirm Readiness
- No ring enabled for untrained users
- Readiness is confirmed per ring, not once
- Shift patterns
- Languages

### 6.5 Post-Deployment Verification
- No release closed without a production check
- Mismatches become defects, problems or ADR updates
- Every release gets a retrospective
- Flags removed on a scheduled date
- Soak length
- Operations acceptance criteria

### 6.5.1 Run Smoke Checks
- No exposure before smoke passes
- Smoke never uses real customer data
- Synthetic checks stay on after the release
- No real data in smoke

### 6.5.2 Verify Production Against Predictions
- A release is not closed without a production check
- Claims cite numbers, not adjectives
- Mismatches become defects, problems or ADR updates — never notes
- Soak length
- Measurement maturity

### 6.5.3 Run Hypercare
- Every defect routed to the backlog with severity and owner
- The building team stays on hand during hypercare
- Team availability

### 6.5.4 Close the Release & Hand Over to OPERATE
- Closed only after the production check and soak
- Change record closed with its outcome
- Every release gets a retrospective
- Operations acceptance criteria

# AGENTS.md — {{initiative}}

> Node SDLC · Act VI RELEASE · Scale: Platform. Read this first, every session.

## How we work
People own the work, agents help do it. In every unit the person in the role briefs the agent, gives it the right context, checks what it produces, and makes every decision. The agent drafts, researches, analyses, structures and checks — it never decides, approves or signs.
- **You:** Choose what to work on · give context · make decisions · review and correct · sign off · own the artifact
- **Your agent:** Draft · research · summarise · structure into templates · spot gaps and risks · check against criteria · prepare options

## Where this act sits
RELEASE is part of the **Delivery track** — Are we building the thing right? The acts keep their order as a logical dependency — a problem is validated before it is planned, designed before it is built — but they are kinds of work that run continuously and in parallel, at different sizes, not phases on a calendar.

## RELEASE: Move verified change into production safely, reversibly and on a recorded decision, with the organisation ready to support it.
- **6.1 Release Prep & Change Approval** — gate: Go / No-Go. Produces: Release candidate, Change record, Release notes, Go / No-Go decision record, Conditions register.
- **6.2 Deployment** — gate: Deployed with Rollback Proven. Produces: Deployment plan, Rollback plan, Staging rehearsal record, Deployment record, Rollback record.
- **6.3 Progressive Rollout** — gate: Full Exposure. Produces: Exposure plan, Guardrail definitions, Ring record, Flag change log.
- **6.4 Launch Readiness** — gate: Launch Readiness. Produces: Support enablement pack, Communications plan, User documentation, Training record, Launch readiness record.
- **6.5 Post-Deployment Verification** — gate: Release Closed. Produces: Smoke check results, Post-deployment verification report, Hypercare log, Operational handover pack, Release record, Release retrospective, Learning log.
- Act gate: **Go / No-Go** — decided by: Release manager decides go / no-go and ring promotion; sponsor is the release authority for disputes; on-call may pull the kill switch without asking..

## Conventions
- Artifacts live in `docs/<artifact>.md`, written from `templates/<artifact>.md`.
- Every artifact carries its trace ID and links the IDs upstream of it; register new IDs in `TRACE.md`.
- Trace chain: RC → CHG → GNG → DEP → RING → LCH → RN → PDV → LRN.
- Log each step in `PROGRESS.md`.
- Before saving, score the artifact against `rubrics/<artifact>.md`.

## Your toolkit
- `commands/` — one per step, workflow, subprocess, process and the act. Start with `release-run-act` or the unit you're on.
- `workflows/` — run specs with checkpoints; stop at every checkpoint.
- `skills/` — how-to packages for each technique; load the ones a command names.
- `agents/` — reviewers by lens, plus researcher, synthesiser, challenger and decision-brief writer.
- `TOOLS.md` and `GUARDRAILS.md` — what you may use and must never do.

## Ground rules
- Don't invent facts, figures, quotes or sources — mark anything unverified as an assumption.
- If something you need is missing, ask me instead of guessing.
- Keep personal or confidential data out unless I've provided it for this purpose.
- Prepare decisions; don't make them — I decide.

## Scale: Platform
Treat other internal teams as the customers. Capture their needs as service or API contracts, and consider versioning, backward compatibility, self-service, documentation and adoption.
Access: Read and write the platform repository and API docs in branches; consuming teams' systems are read-only.

# Guardrails & hooks — Release

People own the work, agents help do it. In every unit the person in the role briefs the agent, gives it the right context, checks what it produces, and makes every decision. The agent drafts, researches, analyses, structures and checks — it never decides, approves or signs.

## Always
- Don't invent facts, figures, quotes or sources — mark anything unverified as an assumption.
- If something you need is missing, ask me instead of guessing.
- Keep personal or confidential data out unless I've provided it for this purpose.
- Prepare decisions; don't make them — I decide.
- Never paste passwords, keys, or personal data you aren't allowed to share — anonymise first
- At enterprise scale, use only approved tools
- Check every fact, number and source the agent gives you
- Agents prepare decisions; people make them
- Save the output in the artifact template and note that an agent helped
- If the agent's output is wrong, correct the prompt or the context — then record what you learned

## Scale: Platform
- Read and write the platform repository and API docs in branches; consuming teams' systems are read-only.
- Watch for: Building what the platform team finds interesting, not what consumers need
- Watch for: Breaking changes without versioning

## Hooks — automatic where your agent supports them, a checklist everywhere else
| When | Check | If it fails |
|---|---|---|
| Before saving an artifact | It follows its template · it carries its trace ID and links upstream IDs · every claim cites evidence or is marked 'Assumption:' · no personal data or secrets | Fix, or stop and tell me |
| Before a decision step | Stop. Prepare the decision brief. Wait for the named decision-maker | Never decide or approve |
| Before anything leaves the team | Messages, posts, invitations and shared documents are drafts until a person sends them | Ask for approval |
| Before using a new tool or data source | Is it allowed at this scale? Is the data allowed in this tool? | Ask first |
| After each step | Append to PROGRESS.md: date, unit, what was done, artifacts, decisions, open questions, next | Always |

## Rules and policies by unit
### RELEASE
- A go — named person, date, outcome — is the only thing that makes stories Released
- Scope (only verified stories) is never conditional
- Every condition has an owner, evidence and a due date
- Every rollback raises a problem record; every release, including a rolled-back one, ends with a retrospective
- Change management per ISO/IEC 20000-1
- No exposure before support, comms, docs and training are ready
- Change windows and freezes
- Decision rights

### 6.1 Release Prep & Change Approval
- Scope is never conditional
- A go is the only thing that makes stories Released
- Change policy per ISO/IEC 20000-1
- Decider named before the release
- Change windows and freezes

### 6.1.1 Assemble the Release Candidate
- A story cannot be in two open releases
- Scope — only verified stories — is never conditional
- Requesters of excluded work are told before deployment
- Only verified stories
- The release window

### 6.1.2 Raise & Approve the Change
- No production change without an approved change record
- Emergency changes reviewed within two working days
- Change policy per ISO/IEC 20000-1
- Security review for new data flows
- Change freezes
- Business peak hours

### 6.1.3 Write Release Notes
- Never describe what is not in the build
- Plain language, written for each audience
- Release scope

### 6.1.4 Hold the Go / No-Go Decision
- Scope — only verified stories — is never conditional
- A go is the only thing that makes stories Released
- A no-go names what must change
- The decider is named before the release, not during it
- Release window
- Decision rights

### 6.2 Deployment
- No deployment without a recorded go and an approved change
- No manual changes in production
- Build once, deploy many
- Deploy outside business peaks
- Change window
- Data migrations

### 6.2.1 Plan the Deployment & Rollback
- No manual changes in production
- No contract migration in the same release as its expand
- Build once, deploy many
- Window length
- Data migrations

### 6.2.2 Rehearse & Prove Rollback
- An unrehearsed rollback fails the Go / No-Go
- Rehearse every release, not only the 'big' ones
- Staging parity

### 6.2.3 Deploy to Production
- No deployment without a recorded go and an approved change
- No hand edits in production
- Deploy outside business peaks
- Change window

### 6.2.4 Roll Back or Roll Forward
- Roll back first, diagnose later
- A roll-forward is a new change with its own go
- Every rollback raises a problem record
- Time to restore

### 6.3 Progressive Rollout
- Thresholds set before exposure and never moved after
- One ring at a time
- Every release flag has an owner and a removal date
- Site freezes
- Open conditions

### 6.3.1 Configure Flags & Exposure Plan
- Thresholds are set before exposure and never moved after
- Every release flag has an owner and a removal date
- Site freezes
- Flag capability in the build

### 6.3.2 Run Ring 0 (Canary)
- Never promote on a breached threshold
- Ring 0 users are trained and know how to report
- Soak time
- Pilot volume

### 6.3.3 Promote Through the Rings
- One ring at a time
- No promotion inside a freeze
- Users told and trained before their ring
- Freezes
- Open conditions

### 6.3.4 Watch Guardrails, Pause or Roll Back
- Rollback threshold breached → roll back, no debate
- Every pause and resume logged
- Pre-agreed thresholds

### 6.4 Launch Readiness
- No ring enabled for untrained or unsupported users
- Localised for every site in scope
- WCAG 2.2 AA for user documentation
- Translation lead time
- Shift patterns

### 6.4.1 Enable Support
- No exposure before support is briefed
- Hypercare length and exit criteria set in advance
- Support capacity

### 6.4.2 Plan & Send Launch Communications
- Never announce a date a ring hasn't confirmed
- Localised for each site
- Ring dates

### 6.4.3 Publish User & Operational Documentation
- Docs versioned with the release
- Localised for every site in scope
- Translation lead time

### 6.4.4 Train Users & Confirm Readiness
- No ring enabled for untrained users
- Readiness is confirmed per ring, not once
- Shift patterns
- Languages

### 6.5 Post-Deployment Verification
- No release closed without a production check
- Mismatches become defects, problems or ADR updates
- Every release gets a retrospective
- Flags removed on a scheduled date
- Soak length
- Operations acceptance criteria

### 6.5.1 Run Smoke Checks
- No exposure before smoke passes
- Smoke never uses real customer data
- Synthetic checks stay on after the release
- No real data in smoke

### 6.5.2 Verify Production Against Predictions
- A release is not closed without a production check
- Claims cite numbers, not adjectives
- Mismatches become defects, problems or ADR updates — never notes
- Soak length
- Measurement maturity

### 6.5.3 Run Hypercare
- Every defect routed to the backlog with severity and owner
- The building team stays on hand during hypercare
- Team availability

### 6.5.4 Close the Release & Hand Over to OPERATE
- Closed only after the production check and soak
- Change record closed with its outcome
- Every release gets a retrospective
- Operations acceptance criteria

# Workflow 6.1.1.1 · Assemble the Release Candidate

Assemble the release story by story from verified increments, with an objective, explicit exclusions and owners for every dependency and gate condition.

**Run it:** ask your agent to "run `workflows/release-6-1-1-1-assemble-rc.md` for {{initiative}}, stopping at every checkpoint", or use the command `release-6-1-1-1-run-assemble-rc`. Each checkpoint means: show me the output and wait. At `decision` checkpoints the named person decides.

```yaml
workflow: release-6-1-1-1-assemble-rc
title: "Assemble the Release Candidate"
owner: "Release manager"
inputs:
  - "docs/quality-gate-record.md"
  - "docs/verified-increment.md"
  - "docs/build-artifact.md"
preconditions:
  - "Quality gate passed or conditionally passed"
  - "Release build in the registry"
steps:
  - id: s1
    do: "Write the release objective"
    owner: "Release manager"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: release-6-1-1-1-s1-write-the-release-objective
    reviewers: [product-reviewer]
    output: "docs/release-candidate.md"
    checkpoint: review
  - id: s2
    do: "Pick verified stories"
    owner: "Release manager"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: release-6-1-1-1-s2-pick-verified-stories
    skills: [build-once-deploy-many]
    reviewers: [devops-reviewer, customer-reviewer]
    output: "docs/release-candidate.md"
    checkpoint: review
    on:
```
